_meta.purpose: Methodology-level findings about this skill itself. Not a model family. Lives alongside per-family files so the dialectical record covers the framework too.
_meta.last_updated: 2026-08-27 (_meta-111 through _meta-114: stream-agnostic build completion, execution-input sealing, CI environment equivalence, and EXHAUSTED-FAIL tuples)
_meta.architecture_note: This skill was refactored from a two-agent (producer + reviewer/REVIEW.md) into a six-agent pipeline, driven by an orchestrator (seven role files total under agents/). Role-to-step map: orchestrator is the entry point + loop driver + per-model isolation owner (_meta-043/_meta-044), planner owns Step 0/1/1b, producer owns Step 2/3/5, tester owns the Goal-ladder march, learner owns Step 4/4b/4c, explainer owns Step 6/7, reviewer is the independent post-PR verifier (formerly REVIEW.md). Historical findings below were written under the old structure; their terminology has been migrated but the dialectical reasoning that motivated the split is preserved.
_meta.epistemics_warning: These are observations about the skill (SKILL.md + the six agent role files under agents/), not about any model. Update when the skill's own claims are refuted.

findings.title: Initial SKILL.md mis-located the per-architecture code surface — caught and corrected during the 12-model methodology test
findings.observation: The first draft of SKILL.md (2026-06-22 morning) directed contributors to src/winml/modelkit/export/ for per-architecture exporter files. Applying the diagnostic step to 12 candidate models surfaced that this directory contains only generic plumbing (pytorch.py, io.py, value_range.py) — the real per-architecture surface is src/winml/modelkit/models/hf/<model_type>.py, where each file registers `OnnxConfig` subclasses via `@register_onnx_overwrite` and optionally `WinMLCompositeModel` subclasses via `@register_composite_model`. SKILL.md Step 2 + 'Where the code lives' table were corrected the same day.

validated_on: repo @ 2026-06-22 commit 4c8428f0

gotchas: Path-truth check belongs in Step 1 (diagnostic): a real contributor running `winml inspect` would not have hit the wrong path — but a contributor reading SKILL.md offline (e.g. before installing winml) would. Both flows are valid. Cite directory listings in the skill itself, not only in the diagnostic step.

The CLAUDE.md prohibition on hardcoded paths in source code does NOT extend to SKILL.md documentation paths — but those paths drift the same way and should be re-verified each time the skill is touched.

findings.title: Step-1 diagnostic missed the Optimum vendor registry — 4 of 6 'needs new code' families were already covered by Optimum, mis-classifying them as L1/L2 instead of L0★
findings.observation:
Second iteration of the 12-model audit (2026-06-22 PM) added an Optimum-coverage probe (temp/probe_optimum_coverage.py, snapshot of TasksManager._SUPPORTED_MODEL_TYPE[mt]['onnx'].keys() before vs after ensure_hf_models_registered()). Results saved to temp/coverage_report.json. Verdicts for the 6 families originally classified as needing new winml code:
  - bart 'text-classification' — VENDOR-ONLY (Optimum's BartOnnxConfig registers 8 tasks natively, bart-large-mnli is L0★ not L1)
  - m2m_100 'text2text-generation' — VENDOR-ONLY (Optimum's M2M100OnnxConfig covers it, NLLB is L0★ not L1)
  - pix2struct 'image-to-text' — VENDOR-ONLY (Optimum's Pix2StructOnnxConfig handles variable-patch internally, deplot/ai2d/docvqa are L0★/L1 not L2)
  - mgp-str 'feature-extraction' — VENDOR-ONLY for encoder, image-to-text still needs L1-light winml override (3-head outputs)
  - vilt — UNREGISTERED in both vendor and winml (true L1 confirmed)
  - depth_pro — WINML-ONLY (true L0★ confirmed)
Four of the six families were mis-classified upward in the first iteration because Step-1 only grepped src/winml/modelkit/models/hf/, never asked Optimum what it covers natively. A 'no winml registration' result was conflated with 'no registration anywhere'.

validated_on: optimum @ probe 2026-06-22 against TasksManager._SUPPORTED_MODEL_TYPE
falsified_on: initial Effort-tier classifications in m2m_100-001, pix2struct-001, partially mgp_str-001 and bart-001
not_yet_tested_on: any of the 12 candidate models against an actual `winml build` execution

gotchas: The keyset diff (vendor task-keys before vs after winml registration) detects added tasks but NOT class-identity overrides. marian had added_by_winml=[] despite the file containing @register_onnx_overwrite for two tasks — because overwrite_existing=True replaces the partial under the SAME key. A true 'is winml overriding?' check requires comparing cls.__qualname__ per (model_type, task) cell, not just keys.
Optimum normalizes model_type with both hyphen and underscore in HF configs. mgp-str (hyphen) is registered; mgp_str (underscore) is not. Always probe both variants.

Optimum's coverage for a task is necessary but NOT sufficient for winml. Goal-L1 (perf gate) may force an L0★ → L1-light promotion if the vendor's DynamicCache-style decoder export is HTP-unfriendly on QNN NPU. Decision should be data-driven via `winml perf` against the vanilla Optimum export, NOT pre-emptive.

Net effect: the first-pass methodology over-estimated effort because it only saw half the registry. A diagnostic that misses 'work already done by upstream' is worse than no diagnostic — it sends contributors to write code they don't need.

findings.title: Goal-L0 verification command in SKILL.md was wrong — surfaced only by actually running the skill end-to-end on apple/DepthPro-hf
findings.observation: First end-to-end exercise of the skill (depth_pro-002, 2026-06-22 PM) ran `winml inspect -m temp/depth_pro_build/model.onnx --format json` as Goal-L0 acceptance per the SKILL.md table. inspect refused with 'Error: ONNX file inspection is not yet supported. Use winml config -m model.onnx for ONNX build config.' The Goal-L0 row had been written from imagination, not from running the verifier. Substituted `python -c "import onnx; m = onnx.load(...)"` for shape/opset validation, which worked. Separately, `winml build` exited with PowerShell exit code 1 despite the build completing cleanly — a benign OpenVINO EP DLL load failure on stderr propagated through `2>&1 | Tee-Object` and poisoned the exit code. CI/scripted consumers cannot trust `winml`'s exit code today.

validated_on: depth_pro-002 build run @ 2026-06-22 PM with winml-cli @ HEAD
falsified_on: SKILL.md Goal-L0 row as authored in iter-1

gotchas: Iter-3 and iter-4 of this skill's methodology test were both pure paper exercises (probe scripts, table edits, finding-file appends). Neither would have caught either bug — only an actual `winml build` invocation exposed them. Lesson: every methodology iteration owes at least one end-to-end run, otherwise the methodology grades itself.

The Goal-L0 row had a syntactically reasonable command that any reader (and any agent) would have accepted on inspection — 'winml inspect <artifact>' parallels 'winml inspect <model-id>'. Plausibility ≠ correctness. SKILL.md should cite the command source (commit / output) when it documents a verification command.

Historical guidance required parsing stdout for '✅ Build complete'. `_meta-111` supersedes that stream-specific rule: require exit 0, final-artifact existence, structural validation, and the marker in captured combined output or its expected Rich stderr stream.

FILE: winml-cli swallow benign EP-install/registration errors so exit code reflects the actual command outcome — today scripted consumers and CI cannot use `$LASTEXITCODE`.
findings.mechanism_notes: Both gaps reproduced and quoted from temp/depth_pro_build.log on 2026-06-22 PM.
findings.resolution: SKILL.md Goal-L0 row was rewritten 2026-06-22 PM to use `onnx.load` for artifact validation and to explicitly call out that `winml inspect` is HF-model-ID-only. The former stdout-only completion rule is superseded by `_meta-111` and the active planner/tester/reviewer artifact-gated contract.

findings.title: Artifact mining is mandatory before knowledge capture; the accompanying README prescription was historical and is superseded
findings.observation: After running depth_pro end-to-end (depth_pro-002, 2026-06-22 PM), I wrote a finding that captured ONE thing: 'build succeeded in 758s, artifact loads, here's the I/O shape'. The user asked '你有没有把知识落地下来?' (did you actually capture knowledge?) and forced me to look at the build outputs. I had ignored THREE structured JSONs sitting in temp/depth_pro_build/: analyze_result.json (per-EP op support), export_htp_metadata.json (module hierarchy, parameter count, trace coverage), winml_build_config.json (autoconf-resolved config). Each contained model-specific structural knowledge worth recording: '3 independent DINOv2 backbones', '49% layout-move ops', 'autoconf picked gelu+matmul-add only'. None of that landed in the first-pass finding. I also forgot to add a row to examples/recipes/README.md — a published recipe that no contributor can discover via the index is half-shipped. Step 4 of SKILL.md says 'append to model_knowledge/<family>.json' but doesn't enumerate WHAT to mine.

validated_on: depth_pro-002 first-pass capture vs depth_pro-003 second-pass capture @ 2026-06-22 PM
falsified_on: SKILL.md Step 4 as authored (too vague)

gotchas: Side observation about analyze_result.json from the same run: the analyze step ran ONLY against DmlExecutionProvider (because that was the system's default device probe), and all 19 op types came back classification=unknown because DML EP runtime_support=False on this box. So the artifact looks like it carries per-EP support data but actually carries one EP probe that failed. Anyone reading analyze_result.json without checking which EP it covers will be misled. SKILL.md should tell the contributor to (a) re-run analyze with the EP they actually care about and (b) treat all-unknown as 'EP unavailable', not 'op unsupported'.

Historical correction: do not update `examples/recipes/README.md`; `_meta-069` made it a forbidden production index. Discoverability comes from the tested `<ep>/<device>` recipe path and PR/report metadata.

The 952M-param + 3-independent-DINOv2-backbones architecture insight has direct quantization consequences: a calibration dataset feeding only the top-level model leaves 2 of 3 backbones uncalibrated. Without mining export_htp_metadata.json no one would know this from looking at the .onnx alone.
feature_gaps_filed: FILE: SKILL.md Step 4 should list the artifacts to mine: temp/<build>/analyze_result.json (op counts + per-EP coverage), temp/<build>/export_htp_metadata.json (module hierarchy + param count + trace coverage ratio), temp/<build>/winml_build_config.json (autoconf-resolved diff against my recipe).
RESOLVED/SUPERSEDED by `_meta-069`: production `examples/recipes/README.md` must remain unchanged.
FILE: winml-cli analyze should default to ALL available EPs on the host, not silently fall back to one. Or expose a clear 'EP unavailable' classification distinct from 'op unknown'.
findings.mechanism_notes: Reproduction trail: depth_pro-002 finding (first pass, sparse) → user challenge → read 3 JSON artifacts → depth_pro-003 finding (structural data) + README index row. All on 2026-06-22 PM.
findings.resolution: Artifact-mining checklist remains authoritative and is still cited by learner/explainer/reviewer. The historical README-index requirement is superseded by `_meta-069`; current contributions must not modify that production index.

findings.title: Producer-only self-grading — the failure that motivated splitting the workflow into the six-agent pipeline (producer ≠ tester ≠ reviewer; reviewer contract now in agents/reviewer.md)
findings.observation: Two consecutive same-day failures (_meta-005 fabricated verification command, _meta-006 missed artifact mining) both share root cause: a single agent was the only verifier. That one agent authored the skill doc, ran the skill, wrote the finding, and judged whether the finding was complete. The user's challenge '你有没有把知识落地下来?' is exactly what an external reviewer would have asked structurally. First resolution: split the workflow into a producer (Steps 0-5) and a reviewer (a fail-closed checklist). This later generalized into the current six-agent pipeline — planner/producer/tester/learner/explainer/reviewer — so that the agent that produces an artifact is never the agent that grades it. The reviewer is bound to (a) re-run at least one command from the PR, (b) read the 3 build artifacts directly rather than trust the producer's summary, (c) re-run the Optimum-coverage probe and cross-check the claimed Effort tier, (d) reject if any claimed verification command can't actually run today (e.g. `winml inspect <artifact>.onnx`).

validated_on: depth_pro contribution sequence on 2026-06-22 PM: _meta-005 and _meta-006 both surfaced only after user challenge

gotchas: This finding was itself produced without a reviewer agent. The first reviewer-agent invocation IS the validation — until that happens, agents/reviewer.md is a hypothesis just like any other finding. Mark `mechanism_confirmed: false` until a real reviewer pass exists.

The reviewer agent must NOT be a different instance of the same agent fed the same workspace context, because that instance shares the producer's mental shortcuts. A separate session / separate agent with only the PR diff and agents/reviewer.md as inputs is the strongest form. A weaker form (same agent in 'reviewer mode' starting from a fresh checkout) is the minimum.

agents/reviewer.md's 'Self-check before issuing a verdict' guidance exists specifically to defend against rubber-stamp reviews. If the reviewer can't name a command they re-ran, the review is paperwork and the verdict is invalid.

Risk: agents/reviewer.md's checklist may itself drift out of sync with the other agent files. Anchor each check to a specific agent-file row or a `_meta-NNN` finding so changes propagate together. If an agent-file row is edited without a matching agents/reviewer.md update, that's a separate bug worth a follow-up finding.

FILE: when a skill change (SKILL.md or any agents/*.md) is reviewed (not just a model contribution), the reviewer should additionally verify the change has been exercised end-to-end at least once — paper edits to the skill docs are how the methodology grades itself.

The tester (agents/tester.md) owns the in-loop Goal-ladder verification before the PR exists. Confirmed by the first independent reviewer passes (see _meta-011, _meta-034).

findings.title: Optimum-coverage probe is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT — vendor coverage does not imply a build will succeed
findings.observation: Iter-5 trial (2026-06-22 PM) ran the new producer/reviewer split (now the six-agent pipeline) against the iter-1 candidate sheet. facebook/bart-large-mnli, classified as L0★ by iter-4's Optimum-coverage probe (vendor BartOnnxConfig covers text-classification), build FAILED at the export stage with `Error: Build failed: index -1 is out of bounds for dimension 1 with size 0`. Root-cause hypothesis (bart-003): BartForSequenceClassification.forward pools encoder hidden state at the last eos_token_id position; random int32 dummy input never contains an eos token; nonzero() returns empty; [-1] indexing throws. The Optimum-coverage probe answers 'does the OnnxConfig exist?' — it does NOT answer 'does the DummyInputGenerator produce inputs that exercise the forward without tripping checkpoint-specific assertions?'. SKILL.md Step 1's verdict table maps probe results to Effort tiers, but those Effort tiers are LOWER BOUNDS — a probe-says-L0★ contribution can still be effectively L1 if the upstream DummyInputGenerator is wrong.

validated_on: facebook/bart-large-mnli @ text-classification @ cpu (2026-06-22 PM, bart-003)
not_yet_tested_on: other eos-pooling NLI checkpoints (xlm-roberta-large-xnli, deberta-v3-large-mnli) — do they hit the same dummy-input issue?

gotchas: The probe verdict 'VENDOR-ONLY' should be read as 'on paper, no winml code is needed'. The probe verdict 'VENDOR-ONLY + build succeeds' is the actually-actionable signal. Without the build, the probe is at best a planning artifact.

_meta-004 (the iter-4 finding that introduced the probe) implicitly conflated these. The probe was framed as 'determines Effort tier', not 'narrows the candidate Effort tier subject to the dummy input working'. Update _meta-004's gotchas: a build attempt with the producer's dummy-input generator is the only definitive signal.
feature_gaps_filed: FILE: SKILL.md Step 1 verdict table should add a row 'Probe says VENDOR-ONLY but build fails on random dummy input' → likely a head-specific assertion (eos-pooling, padded-position lookup, ...) and the contribution becomes L1-light to fix the DummyInputGenerator.

FILE: agents/reviewer.md should add an explicit check: 'If the producer claims L0★, the reviewer MUST re-run the build, not just confirm the recipe exists' — already implied by the existing 'Build re-runs cleanly' box, but the L0★ → build-failure pattern is sneaky enough to deserve its own row.

Marian (also VENDOR-ONLY per the probe) succeeded on the same run, ruling out an environmental cause.
findings.resolution: Captured as bart-003 in model_knowledge/bart.json with full mechanism. SKILL.md Step 1 verdict-table refinement is the next producer's job (and the obvious thing for a reviewer agent to demand). Until then, treat the probe as a planning hint only.

findings.title: `winml config` can dead-end BEFORE producing any recipe draft for variable-shape models — SKILL.md Step 0 assumes a draft always exists
findings.observation: Iter-5 (2026-06-22 PM) ran `uv run winml config -m google/pix2struct-ai2d-base --task image-to-text -o temp/probe_drafts/pix2struct_draft.json`. Command exited with: 'Error: Preprocessors for pix2struct need to be available for the ONNX export to infer input static shapes. Got: None'. No config_draft.json was produced. The error originates inside Optimum (the OnnxConfig knows it needs the Pix2StructProcessor's max_patches to derive flattened_patches shape, and refuses to invent one), and winml does not currently load AutoProcessor and pass its size attributes through. This is BEFORE any build attempt — SKILL.md Step 0's implicit assumption that 'pick a tier, run `winml config`, get a starting recipe' is violated. Affected family: any image-task model with variable input shape (pix2struct, donut variants, fuyu).

validated_on: google/pix2struct-ai2d-base @ image-to-text @ config-stage (2026-06-22 PM, pix2struct-003)
not_yet_tested_on: donut variants
fuyu
kosmos-2 with image-input variant

A reviewer agent would correctly point out that the L0★ verdict-table row says 'task in vendor ⇒ L0★' — not 'L0★ IF `winml config` cooperates'.

The fix is plumbing in `winml config` (load AutoProcessor, pass its size attrs to the OnnxConfig constructor). Until then, the SKILL.md user has to know to either (a) use --processor-args (verify if it exists) or (b) hand-write the recipe — neither path is documented today.

findings.title: Reviewer subagent without terminal-execution capability cannot satisfy agents/reviewer.md's "re-run at least one command" rule — first real reviewer invocation surfaced this
findings.observation: First real exercise of the producer/reviewer split (now the six-agent pipeline) (iter-5 reviewer pass, 2026-06-22 PM, Explore subagent): the reviewer agent issued an honest REQUEST_CHANGES verdict but acknowledged it ran 0 terminal commands. The Explore agent is a read-only subagent (file_search / read_file / grep_search only), and agents/reviewer.md's "Self-check before issuing a verdict" requires re-running at least one of the producer's commands. The reviewer satisfied the spirit of the check by reading the producer's checked-in build artifacts (analyze_result.json, export_htp_metadata.json, winml_build_config.json) and the committed build log — but the literal requirement ("re-run") was not met. _meta-007's resolution claim ("agents/reviewer.md is a hypothesis until a real reviewer pass exists") is now half-validated: the workflow caught real producer defects (5 actionable items), but the tool budget required to fully execute agents/reviewer.md was missing.

validated_on: iter-5 reviewer pass on 2026-06-22 PM with Explore subagent
not_yet_tested_on: any reviewer agent invocation with terminal access (e.g. the same main agent in 'reviewer mode' but with run_in_terminal enabled)

gotchas: agents/reviewer.md as written implicitly assumes the reviewer has the same tool budget as the producer. In practice, subagents are often constrained read-only for safety. The checklist should split into two columns: REQUIRED-FROM-EVIDENCE (file reads, log inspection) vs REQUIRED-FROM-RE-EXECUTION (build, analyze, perf).

A read-only reviewer is still vastly better than no reviewer — the iter-5 reviewer caught the broken bart recipe, the schema misstatement, the pix2struct workaround gap, the batch-mode self-grading. Don't reject the workflow because the tool budget was incomplete; document the constraint.

findings.title: HISTORICAL observation: a quant:null fp16-named recipe built FLOAT weights when no fp16 CLI precision was requested
findings.observation: After Goal-L0/L1 validation of Helsinki-NLP/opus-mt-fr-en, inspected the actual encoder ONNX weight dtypes: `Counter({FLOAT(1): 102, INT64(7): 32})` — zero FLOAT16. findings.title: `winml perf` uses RANDOM dummy inputs at perf-time independent of recipe `value_range` narrowing — eos-pooling / special-token-indexing models crash at perf even when their recipe builds. Workaround = custom Python perf script. First surfaced via bart-004.
findings.observation: After fixing bart-large-mnli's build with `value_range:[2,3]` for input_ids (bart-004), ran `winml perf -m examples/recipes/facebook_bart-large-mnli/text-classification_config.json --ep cpu --iterations 30 --warmup 5` — perf crashed at the first iteration with the SAME `Gather indices=-1` error that bart-003 surfaced at build. Investigation: `winml perf`'s dummy-input generator uses random sampling for each iteration and does NOT consult the recipe's `export.input_tensors[*].value_range`. So the build-time workaround does not propagate to perf-time, and 98% of perf iterations re-hit the eos-pooling crash. Fix used for this turn: hand-written perf script (temp/bart_mnli_perf.py) that builds real tokenized inputs via AutoTokenizer + measures latency directly via onnxruntime. 1637ms/iter on real input (vs crash on random input). Pattern is generic to any model whose forward() does positional index lookup on a special token (eos/bos/pad/sep).

validated_on: facebook/bart-large-mnli @ text-classification @ cpu — winml perf crashes with random inputs; custom script succeeds (2026-06-22 PM)
not_yet_tested_on: other eos-pooling NLI checkpoints (xlm-roberta-large-xnli, deberta-v3-large-mnli)
models with bos/sep/pad indexing in forward (e.g. BertForNextSentencePrediction)

gotchas: Build success ≠ perf success when the model has special-token-positional-index logic. Always re-run `winml perf` after a recipe-level workaround that targets dummy-input distribution.

Random perf inputs are the DEFAULT and aren't documented as such anywhere obvious. Contributors who succeed at build then run perf will see a confusing 'this worked yesterday' regression. Mention this prominently in SKILL.md perf section.

Custom-script perf workaround template: `import time, onnxruntime as ort; sess = ort.InferenceSession(path, providers=[ep]); inputs = real_tokenized_inputs(...); [sess.run(None, inputs) for _ in range(warmup)]; t0 = time.perf_counter(); [sess.run(None, inputs) for _ in range(iters)]; print((time.perf_counter()-t0)/iters * 1000, 'ms/iter')`.

Reviewers should NOT auto-reject a recipe whose `winml perf` evidence is a custom Python script instead of the `winml perf` CLI output — for eos-pooling and similar special-token-indexing models, the custom script is the only honest path.

FILE: `winml perf --inputs <path-to-real-input-pkl>` (or similar) flag — let producers supply pre-computed real inputs instead of relying on random sampling.
FILE: the tester Goal-L1 march (agents/tester.md) + agents/reviewer.md Goal-L1 check should both note that custom perf scripts are acceptable evidence for special-token-pooling models.

The honest mid-ladder pause is a REPORT ('L1 PASS; L2 attempt aborted at 3 minutes because <reason>, downgrading Goal ceiling to L1; full evidence in <path>'), not a QUESTION.
A producer who commits to Goal ceiling = L3 and ships only L0+L1 evidence is structurally indistinguishable from one who never committed at all. Both are REQUEST_CHANGES under `_meta-018`.

Short-circuit clarification: a hard `FAIL` at `Lk` halts the march (downgrade ceiling to `L(k-1)`, do NOT attempt `L(k+1)`+). Higher-tier evidence on top of a broken lower tier is meaningless (L2 cosine on an artifact whose L1 perf crashes) or actively misleading (L3 accuracy on an artifact whose L0 silently shipped wrong-precision weights despite an `_fp16_` filename per `_meta-014`). findings.observation: PR#851 documents that `BartForConditionalGeneration` is registered in Optimum as `fill-mask`, which is semantically wrong (it's seq2seq generation). WinML's `_upgrade_fill_mask_for_seq2seq` re-routes `(model_type='bart', task='fill-mask')` to `text2text-generation` when `config.is_encoder_decoder == True`. The correction lives at BOTH detection sites: `_detect_task_from_config` (inspect path) and `_detect_task_and_class_from_config` (build path; both replaced by `resolve_task` per PR#878). My Optimum-coverage probe at SKILL.md Step 1 prints `vendor[mt][onnx].keys()` — it would correctly show `fill-mask` for bart-large-cnn, but my methodology never flagged that the *label* is suspect. A contributor reading the probe output as 'optimum supports fill-mask on bart, great, build it' would ship a recipe with the wrong task tag and the wrong inference class.

findings.title: For >2GB ONNX models, `torch.onnx.export` writes UUID-named `.data` external data files RELATIVE to the export path. Relative export paths leak external data into CWD (PR#853 fixed it inside `HTPExporter._convert_model_to_onnx`). Recipe-authoring and `winml build -o <relative>` documentation should still surface this constraint.
findings.observation: PR#853 (2026-06-10) is a 3-line fix in `src/winml/modelkit/export/htp/exporter.py`: `output_path = Path(output_path).resolve()`. The original issue: `torch.onnx.export` for >2GB models silently writes UUID-named `.data` files alongside the model, and the cwd-vs-output-dir bug scattered these files. The fix is internal to HTPExporter so `winml build -o temp\out\` now works regardless of CWD. BUT — hand-written export scripts (the `temp/*_l2_compare.py` template family SKILL.md endorses for Goal-L2) still pass paths into `onnxruntime.InferenceSession()` and `torch.onnx.export()` and can repeat the bug. My SKILL.md's L2 section never mentions this.

findings.title: `winml perf --memory` (PR#861, default-on) measures RAM + VRAM phase deltas (baseline → model load → inference). Goal-L1 row in SKILL.md cites only latency; big-model contributions should ALSO report memory.
findings.observation: PR#861 (2026-06-16) added a `--memory` / `--no-memory` flag to `winml perf` and made it default-on. Output format: `RAM: <baseline> -> model load: +X | inference: +Y | total: +Z` and `VRAM: <local/shared> -> ...`. Phase boundaries: baseline after `_load_model()`, after `compile()`, after benchmark loop. VRAM uses PDH `\GPU Process Memory` counters. My SKILL.md Goal-L1 row's pass criterion is 'latency reported (Avg / P50 / P90 / P99 / Throughput)' — a contribution that ships a 3.6 GB depth_pro recipe with NO memory data is honoring SKILL.md but not honoring the model-scale dimension the CLI now measures by default.

not_yet_tested_on: pre-PR#861 perf runs that did not capture memory

gotchas: VRAM line only shows when device memory > 0; CPU-only runs see RAM only. Reviewer should NOT REQUEST_CHANGES on a CPU-only run for missing VRAM.
psutil RSS is process-level, includes any pre-existing python heap. Useful for delta but not absolute footprint.

Memory snapshots are between phases (no overhead in measurement window) but mean phase boundaries must be respected; a custom script that doesn't separate compile from inference cannot reproduce the same numbers.
feature_gaps_filed: FILE: SKILL.md Goal-L1 pass criterion must extend to '+ RAM delta per phase + (when applicable) VRAM delta per phase'. Big-model recipes (>500 MB artifact) must report memory.

findings.title: Composite encoder-decoder loop expects the encoder to expose an output called `last_hidden_state`. PR#863 ships an alias-injection so encoders with different output names still work, but hand-written composite recipes with custom output names are still fragile.
findings.observation: PR#863 (2026-06-10) is a 6-line fix in `src/winml/modelkit/models/winml/feature_extraction.py`: 'provide last_hidden_state if the underlying onnx model uses a different output name'. The triggering bug: PR#805 had removed the auto-population, breaking the encoder-decoder composite class. My iter-6 vit-gpt2 encoder declares its output as `encoder_hidden_states` (NOT `last_hidden_state`), and would have broken the composite encoder-decoder loop without #863's alias injection. The fix is at the INFERENCE class layer, not the recipe layer, so authors don't see it.

If composite loop breaks at runtime with 'KeyError: last_hidden_state', the recipe's encoder output name diverged AND the alias-injection didn't catch it.

findings.title: `winml perf --ep-options KEY=VALUE` (PR#865, repeatable) is an independent runtime EP-tuning knob from build-time quant. Big-model L1 failures on NPU/GPU should retry with appropriate options (e.g. QNN `htp_performance_mode=burst`) BEFORE declaring L1 FAIL.
findings.observation: PR#865/#889 (2026-06-16) added `--ep-options KEY=VALUE` to `winml perf`. Options thread through `parse_ep_options() → BenchmarkConfig.ep_options → WinMLAutoModel.from_pretrained / from_onnx → WinMLSession → add_ep_for_device`. Runtime options merge OVER build-time `ep_config.provider_options` and do NOT flip EPContext persistence (`persist_jit`). The QNN HTP example (`htp_performance_mode=burst`) significantly affects latency on Snapdragon NPUs. My SKILL.md Goal-L1 row says only `winml perf -m <artifact>.onnx --device <target> --ep <ep>` — no mention of runtime tuning knobs.

not_yet_tested_on: any recipe attempting L1 on QNN NPU with default options vs `htp_performance_mode=burst`

gotchas: QNN HTP `htp_performance_mode=burst` is the most common option. Other QNN options exist (`htp_graph_finalization_optimization_mode`, etc.).
Runtime options override build-time options BUT don't re-finalize the graph — they tune the runtime, not the compiled artifact.
Goal-L1 contract should be: 'tried default; if SLOW or FAILED, retry with documented EP options before claiming FAIL'. The default-only run is an incomplete L1 attempt for NPU/GPU.
feature_gaps_filed: FILE: the tester Goal-L1 march (agents/tester.md) + agents/reviewer.md Goal-L1 check should both mention `--ep-options`. Per-EP recommended options should be tabulated (`htp_performance_mode=burst` for QNN as the canonical example).

findings.title: Project records eval-time TIMEOUT on big models as checked-in artifacts (`*_eval_result.timeout`) rather than treating them as build failures. Methodology must distinguish 'eval times out at scale' from 'eval failed at correctness' — these are different verdicts.

The project tracks 'this big model still times out on this EP' as DATA, not as a regression. My methodology Goal-L3 row says 'within tolerance, documented in PR' but treats failure as binary; the `*.timeout` convention says 'TIMEOUT is a tracked third state'.

not_yet_tested_on: other large models with output projections at the bottleneck (xlm-roberta-xxl, t5-3b, bart-large-cnn at higher batch)

gotchas: Goal-L3 verdict for big models has THREE states, not two: PASS / FAIL-correctness / TIMEOUT-at-scale. The third is the model-scale verdict; it does NOT block the contribution but does fingerprint the recipe.
TIMEOUT can be EP-specific: xlm-roberta-large fill-mask is PASS on QNN GPU (22e4f303), TIMEOUT on DML GPU (5e4a9b0a). Per-EP tracking is what makes `.timeout` files useful.
Conventionally `<model>/<task>_eval_result.timeout` is empty; the existence-as-data pattern.

findings.title: Producer's working branch may lag `main` by N commits; SKILL.md citations to files/APIs introduced by PRs on `main..HEAD-of-producer-branch` are forward-references, not current-state. Producer MUST classify every PR-citation as (a) IN-BRANCH (file exists, can be tested directly), (b) AHEAD-ON-MAIN (file does not exist yet on producer's branch; finding applies when contributor's branch merges main), or (c) HISTORIC (pre-branch-creation, fully merged everywhere).
findings.observation: While recording `_meta-019` through `_meta-029` from a PR-mining sweep on 2026-06-23, the producer (on branch `shzhen/skills_poc`) cited `src/winml/modelkit/loader/resolution.py` introduced by PR#878 (1d4feca3). VS Code's link-resolver flagged the file as missing. Investigation showed HEAD = `967ddccb` is 7 commits BEHIND `origin/main`; PR#878 is in main but NOT an ancestor of HEAD. Sweep results: 5/10 PRs read are IN-BRANCH (`#850 507c2696`, `#851 fc385310`, `#841 938a4ee3`, `#853 5ead5613`, `#863 22479743`), 5/10 are AHEAD-ON-MAIN (`#861 a8257d4c`, `inspect-composite-ui 2f688a0a`, `#878 1d4feca3`, `#865 58d135ed`, `#866 26fcc880`). Findings `_meta-022, _meta-024, _meta-026, _meta-027` and parts of `_meta-020` reference APIs that don't exist on the producer's working branch. A contributor following SKILL.md on this branch would hit dead links / missing functions and incorrectly conclude the skill is out of date — when in fact it's the branch that's behind.

validated_on: shzhen/skills_poc (HEAD 967ddccb) vs origin/main (489abdd4) on 2026-06-23
not_yet_tested_on: future producer agents working on long-lived branches
PRs that revert/refactor an already-merged change after the producer recorded a finding

gotchas: Before citing a file path in SKILL.md or a finding, verify it exists on the producer's HEAD: `Test-Path <path>` (PowerShell) or `[ -f <path> ]` (bash). Dead links in methodology docs are silent producer-failures.

When a PR removes/renames an API (e.g. #878 removed `detect_task`), SKILL.md must cite BOTH the pre-PR and post-PR names with branch-state guard: 'on branches predating #PR, see <legacy-path>; post-#PR, see <new-path>'.
`git merge-base --is-ancestor <pr-commit> HEAD` is the verification command; exit 0 = in HEAD, exit 1 = ahead on main.

Forward-reference findings are LEGITIMATE — a producer reading PR history learns methodology lessons even from un-merged PRs. They must just be MARKED so the reader knows whether the cited API exists on their branch yet.

findings.title: Methodology-evolution contract: every model-support contribution MUST emit either (a) one or more new `_meta-NNN` findings + matching skill-doc (SKILL.md / agents/*.md) + agents/reviewer.md edits PR-bundled with the model artifact, OR (b) an affirmative 'No methodology friction observed' declaration. Silence is `_meta-007` self-grading failure at the methodology level — reviewer issues REQUEST_CHANGES on absent declaration.
findings.observation: Pre-`_meta-031`, SKILL.md's Step 4 only required `model_knowledge/<family>.json` updates. Step-1 PR-mining and the L132 'file a _meta-NNN+1 in the same PR' clause encoded methodology-evolution duties but neither was wired to a reviewer check or a hand-off item; both were skippable. Result: iter-1..iter-5 (5 prior batch contributions) accumulated 17 `_meta-*` findings entirely through ad-hoc audits by the skill author, not by routine producer work. Iter-6 stress-tested this by running PR-mining + Goal-ladder closure as an explicit meta-experiment and produced 13 new findings (_meta-019..030) plus 7 reviewer checks in agents/reviewer.md — confirming that a producer who is *prompted* to reflect on methodology friction can produce skill-level evolution at the same cadence as model contributions, while a producer who isn't prompted produces zero. The fix: enumerate the 7 friction triggers, make Step 4b a named obligation alongside Step 4, and add a single agents/reviewer.md row whose default verdict on silence is REQUEST_CHANGES.

validated_on: iter-6 meta-experiment 2026-06-23 — PR-mining 10 PRs + Goal-ladder L0..L3 on bart-large-mnli + vit-gpt2 → 13 methodology findings + 7 agents/reviewer.md rows + first L3 PASS in repo
falsified_on: implicit assumption in pre-iter-6 SKILL.md that methodology evolution would happen naturally without a producer obligation
not_yet_tested_on: iter-7 (first contribution under the _meta-031 contract) — will validate whether the 7-trigger taxonomy is complete or needs an 8th trigger row
producer agents without read-access to recent PRs — trigger #7 (PR-mining) may need a fallback for offline-or-restricted producers

gotchas: The 7-trigger taxonomy is descriptive (compiled from iter-1..iter-6 audit history), not prescriptive. Iter-7+ contributions will likely surface trigger #8 — when they do, the producer owes a SKILL.md Step 4b table-edit adding the new row, not a workaround.

Trigger #7 (PR-mining) assumes the producer has read-access to the repo's recent PR history. Producers running against a frozen snapshot or in a restricted environment cannot satisfy #7 — the reviewer must downgrade #7 to 'not-applicable on this host' rather than REQUEST_CHANGES.

The declaration MUST be in the PR description (not buried in a finding's `gotchas`), because the reviewer reads PR description first and gates on it before opening the diff. A `_meta-NNN` cited without a PR-description declaration triggers the 'silence' verdict.

Affirmative 'No methodology friction observed' is NOT a hedge — the reviewer will spot-check by scanning the build log + chat transcript for `--help` invocations, custom-wrapper Python files in `temp/`, hand-stitched composite recipes, and incomplete hand-off packages. A producer who declares (b) dishonestly is in a worse state than one who declares (a) honestly.

gotchas: Lane A (skill-only updates push to working branch) vs Lane B (new model = branch off main) is a hard split. Mixing them — e.g. landing SKILL.md edits in a model PR — forces reviewers into context-switching between code-review and methodology-review modes. The producer who mixes lanes is in REQUEST_CHANGES at hand-off; the fix is to git-revert the skill edits from the model PR and re-commit them on the working branch.

Scope-rule-matching-Effort-tier is enforced at PR time, not at recipe-authoring time. Push-failure escalation: Microsoft Enterprise + classic-PAT-with-90-day-rule frequently rejects push from agent-driven sessions. Producer MUST surface the exact stderr to the user with concrete recovery options, not silently fall back to local-mirror-only. A silent fallback is dishonest closure of the Outcome contract.

The `_meta-033` rule applies even when the user did not explicitly ask for a PR. The default is 'producer opens the PR'; the opt-out is the user saying 'don't push yet'. Reversing the default (asking 'should I push?' before every shipment) is friction the user explicitly objected to in the same conversation that surfaced `_meta-032`.

Defaulting to `gh pr create` for any pushed branch — instead of only Lane B branches — violates this rule.

findings.title: Reviewer-checkout protocol: agents/reviewer.md must instruct reviewer to `gh pr checkout <N>` (or `git checkout <branch>`) BEFORE scoring L0..L3, then restore producer branch on completion. Without this step the reviewer scores the producer's possibly-dirty working tree (with N months of unrelated edits) instead of what maintainers will merge.
findings.observation: Iter-6 first reviewer-side run on PRs #933/#934 (2026-06-23) surfaced that agents/reviewer.md `Inputs you receive` line 1 says 'PR diff or workspace state at HEAD' but never bound the reviewer to explicitly switch to the PR head. The reviewer was already on `shzhen/skills_poc` (producer working branch) which contains 12 untracked items + the full `research/` tree that are NOT in the PR diff. A naive reviewer would have scored the working tree, conflating 'recipe works on shzhen/skills_poc' with 'recipe works on the PR scope against main'. Fix: add Step 0 'Check out the actual PR branch (Lane B reviews)' with stash/checkout/diff-scope/restore protocol, including the artifact-reuse rule (if producer's cached build was built BEFORE the PR branch was cut, verify recipe is byte-identical at PR HEAD before reusing artifacts).

validated_on: iter-6 PR #933 (bart-large-mnli) + PR #934 (vit-gpt2) reviewer runs 2026-06-23 — Step 0 protocol exercised end-to-end: stash README → checkout PR branch → diff scope check → L0..L3 re-run from cached artifacts (verified recipe byte-identical) → restore producer branch → stash pop
falsified_on: implicit pre-`_meta-034` assumption that 'reviewer reads the workspace state' is unambiguous — there are at least 3 possible workspace states (producer's working branch with untracked files, the PR branch checked out fresh, main + PR diff applied as a worktree). Each gives different L0..L3 results in the presence of stale untracked artifacts.
not_yet_tested_on: L1+ PRs where the reviewer must rebuild from scratch because no cached artifacts exist or because the recipe diff is non-empty between cached-build commit and PR HEAD
PRs whose branch is force-pushed mid-review — reviewer may need to re-run Step 0 after the producer addresses REQUEST_CHANGES

gotchas: Producer's `temp/verify_<model>_build/` is gitignored — it survives branch checkouts. Reviewer who checks out a different PR branch can REUSE these artifacts IF the recipe at PR HEAD is byte-identical to the recipe the producer built from. Verify with `git diff <cached-commit>..HEAD -- examples/recipes/<org>_<model>/` first. Skip reuse if non-empty.

Working tree with untracked files survives `git checkout` cleanly UNLESS the destination branch tracks one of those paths. If `git checkout` fails with 'would be overwritten by checkout', that's a hidden conflict between an untracked working-tree file and a tracked file on the destination branch — stash the conflicting paths individually (`git stash push -m '...' <paths>`) rather than the whole working tree.

Restore step is non-optional. A reviewer who finishes scoring on the PR branch and then `git commit`s skill updates from there will accidentally push the skill updates to the PR branch (Lane B = recipe-only scope leakage, REQUEST_CHANGES under `_meta-033`). Always `git checkout <producer-working-branch>` + `git stash pop` before any further edits.
feature_gaps_filed: FILE: `gh pr checkout-and-stash` git alias — a one-shot wrapper that does the stash + checkout + scope-print sequence and prints a one-line 'remember to restore with: git checkout <orig> && git stash pop' reminder.

Two APPROVE verdicts shipped as PR comments.

validated_on: iter-6 PR #933 + #934 reviewer-comment fallback (2026-06-23) — both verdicts posted at https://github.com/microsoft/winml-cli/pull/933#issuecomment-4775278723 and pull/934#issuecomment-4775278822, marked 'APPROVE' in body, maintainer sees them in PR conversation
