findings.title: Low-space recovery must be orchestrator-owned, terminal-run scoped, and manifest-driven
findings.observation: Serial reruns accumulated generated ONNX payloads, private environments, and superseded worktrees until disk pressure threatened later models. A successful terminal cleanup reclaimed approximately 17.59 GB while preserving pushed branches, PR state, and compact evidence, but the behavior existed only as an ad hoc run procedure. Encoding it as a broad cache sweep would risk deleting shared Hugging Face datasets/models, package caches, dirty worktrees, or evidence still needed by another role.
findings.rule_change: The orchestrator checks free space before disk-heavy stages and terminal hand-off. Below a configurable minimum, it runs a deterministic dry-run over explicit terminal-run ownership manifests, then deletes only fixed-kind regenerable candidates until a separate target is reached. Path containment, quiescence, completed dependencies, reparse-point rejection, Git cleanliness/recoverability, and protected shared-cache roots fail closed. If eligible resources cannot reach the target, the pipeline blocks rather than widening deletion.
findings.patch_site: SKILL.md resource retirement; orchestrator automatic low-space recovery; cleanup-run-cache.ps1; response eval
findings.skill_edit: SKILL.md; agents/orchestrator.md; scripts/cleanup-run-cache.ps1; evals/evals.json; skill_meta/findings.json

validated_on: PR #1253 terminal cleanup: 30 generated ONNX payloads and 11 run worktrees removed; approximately 17.59 GB reclaimed while compact evidence and shared caches remained
disposable PowerShell fixtures: dry-run preserved candidates, out-of-root paths blocked, execute removed only declared paths, and deletion stopped after reaching target free space
disposable ownership-marker fixtures: marked build output was removed, an ordinary JSON evidence file was rejected, and the cleanup record remained outside disposable roots
disposable local Git fixture: a clean worktree recoverable from origin/main was removed through git worktree remove; a local-only recovery ref and a dirty worktree were rejected and preserved
disposable junction fixture: a nested reparse point blocked the candidate without traversing or deleting its external target
disposable record fixtures: same-run record updates were idempotent, unrelated JSON was not overwritten, and a junction-backed record path was rejected
falsified_on: low disk alone authorizes deleting a shared cache root
filename patterns are sufficient proof of run ownership
terminal state alone proves a worktree is clean and recoverable
all eligible candidates should be deleted even after enough space is available
not_yet_tested_on: non-Windows hosts

findings.mechanism_notes: The real cleanup established the reclaimable resource classes; disposable fixtures verified the helper's parser, dry-run, containment rejection, execute behavior, and target-stop semantics without touching real caches or model artifacts.
findings.resolution: DONE (contract, helper, and response eval) - automatic cleanup is bounded to explicit terminal-run resources and shared caches remain outside its authority.

findings.title: [SUPERSEDED 2026-07-06 by the draft-PR-first workflow — see agents/explainer.md + _meta-042] User-consent gate before `gh pr create`: producer/reviewer agents automate every step UP TO the PR-creation call, but the ship/no-ship decision is the user's. The producer presents (model + tier claim + reviewer verdict + pre-composed `gh pr create` command) and waits for explicit user approval before firing.
findings.observation: Iter-6 (2026-06-23) producer over-applied `_meta-033`'s 'do not wait to be asked' rule and opened Lane A PR #935 against `main` without user consent. User closed #935 and clarified: '发PR的过程你自动化，但是要不要发是人决定的' (mechanics automatic, decision human). The original `_meta-033` framing collapsed two distinct steps — 'run the review' (cheap, automatable, default-on) vs 'fire `gh pr create`' (cheap to fire, expensive to retract; affects upstream queue). Only the first should auto-run. The second is gated on user 'ship' / 'hold' / 'fix X first' decision. A producer who runs `gh pr create` without that explicit go-ahead is committing the same `_meta-007` self-grading mistake as one who skipped the reviewer step, just at a different layer — here the user, not the reviewer, is the authority being bypassed.

validated_on: iter-6 PR #935 closed by user 2026-06-23 (Lane A skill-only PR opened against `main` without user consent); user verbatim clarification '发PR的过程你自动化，但是要不要发是人决定的'
falsified_on: pre-`_meta-036` SKILL.md Step 7 phrasing 'Ship the PR (do not wait to be asked)' — falsified at the upstream-queue layer; the rule was right for the mechanics, wrong for the decision
not_yet_tested_on: iter-7 first model PR — will producer correctly present the pre-composed command + reviewer verdict and stop, or will it default back to firing `gh pr create` autonomously?
user-explicit 'always ship if reviewer APPROVEs' override — a future user might delegate the ship decision; SKILL.md should still default to gated, with explicit user override required to skip

gotchas: The consent gate applies to `gh pr create` only — NOT to `git push`. The branch must be pushed to `origin` as part of producer prep so the user can act on a real branch (review the commit, push it manually, ship later). Holding the branch local-only defeats the prep.
The reviewer agent runs UNGATED — the user shouldn't have to approve 'run the review'. Review-then-present-then-wait is the correct order.

User answers come in three shapes: 'ship' / '发吧' (run the command), 'hold' / 'don't ship' (leave branch pushed, do nothing), 'fix X first' (amend commit, force-push, re-run reviewer, re-present). Producer must wait for one of the three; anything else is REQUEST_CHANGES on the hand-off itself.

Reviewer-verdict REJECT does NOT auto-cancel the prep — the branch is still pushed, the command is still composed, the user still decides (the user may choose to ship a REJECT-verdict PR with the reviewer feedback inlined as discussion context). The reviewer informs; the user decides.
feature_gaps_filed: FILE: 'always-ship' / 'always-hold' user-preference flag — SKILL.md should support an explicit user-set policy that skips the gate (e.g. for a known-good batch). Until that flag exists, gated-by-default is the safe rule.
findings.mechanism_notes: Mechanism not yet re-tested at the time this finding was written. Iter-7 first contribution after this push is the natural test: producer should prep + present + wait, NOT fire. Confirmation requires (a) producer runs Lane B prep automatically, (b) producer surfaces command + verdict, (c) producer halts, (d) user explicit 'ship' triggers `gh pr create`, (e) no PR opened before step (d). If any of (a)–(e) breaks, file as `_meta-036` falsification.
findings.resolution: SKILL.md Step 7 renamed 'Prepare and ship the PR (user holds the trigger)' (2026-06-23). The Lane B shipment block now ends at `git push` (step 4); `gh pr create` moved into a separate 'User-consent gate' subsection that lists the producer's required hand-off package (tier claim, reviewer verdict, pre-composed command, mirror file path) and the three valid user responses. Self-check checkbox 'PR URL returned by `gh pr create`' replaced with 'pre-composed command shown, NOT yet executed'. Pushed to `shzhen/skills_poc` in the same commit. SUPERSEDED 2026-07-06 by the six-agent refactor: agents/explainer.md now mandates a draft-PR-first workflow — the explainer runs `gh pr create --draft` immediately after the producer pushes, with NO user-consent gate ('Do not wait for reviewer approval or user consent — the draft PR is the mechanism for both'); the DRAFT state itself is the safety mechanism, and `gh pr ready` promotes to ready only on reviewer APPROVE. This consent-gate rule is retained as dialectical history but is no longer operative; see _meta-042.

findings.title: Diligence ladder before declaring `*-BLOCKED`: `HOST-BLOCKED` / `CLI-BLOCKED` / `FAIL` are cheap verdicts for producer, expensive for users (each one is a feature-gap that someone has to triage). Before writing any of them, work a 6-step ladder. Stop at the first step that unblocks; document which step worked.
findings.observation: Across iter-3 through iter-6, several '*-BLOCKED' verdicts were declared on first-failure when a known workaround existed in the per-family knowledge file (`_meta-013` bart eos-pooling, `_meta-017` custom-script L1 evidence, `_meta-026` `--ep-options` retry). The producer had read the knowledge file at Step 1 but did not consult it again at the failure point. Pattern: knowledge-file reading is front-loaded, but failure-recovery is back-loaded — they never re-meet. A lightweight 'before you write BLOCKED, walk this ladder' checklist closes the loop without adding ceremony for the happy path.

validated_on: iter-6 reviewer flow on PR #934 — composite vit-gpt2 perf reported via per-half decoder/encoder direct-name-match (knowledge `_meta-020` recall at failure point); iter-5 bart eos-pooling resolved via knowledge file step 1 retroactive consult
not_yet_tested_on: iter-7 first BLOCKED verdict — will producer walk the ladder and document which step unblocked (or document all 6 failures + file a feature-gap)? If producer writes BLOCKED without naming the ladder steps tried, falsifies the rule — the ladder needs more teeth (e.g. reviewer auto-REQUEST_CHANGES on missing ladder trace).

gotchas: The ladder is a list, not a flowchart — stop at first success. Don't waste cycles on steps 4–6 if step 1 (re-read knowledge file) unblocks.

Step 7 (file feature-gap entry) is what makes a BLOCKED verdict honest. A BLOCKED with no `feature_gaps_filed[]` is `_meta-007` self-grading 'I tried' without evidence; the gap entry forces naming what the tool needs to make the case work.

The ladder lives in Step 4c — BEFORE Step 5 (pitfalls) and Step 6 (reviewer hand-off) — because BLOCKED verdicts get baked into the hand-off package. Catching them upstream saves the reviewer round-trip.
feature_gaps_filed: FILE: agents/reviewer.md row to validate 'BLOCKED verdict cites ladder steps tried + feature_gap entry' — currently the reviewer can only flag missing methodology learnings, not missing diligence trace on a BLOCKED verdict.
findings.mechanism_notes: Mechanism not yet tested at write time. Next BLOCKED verdict in iter-7 is the test — producer should either walk the ladder and find a success (in which case the verdict isn't BLOCKED), or walk all 6 and document each + file a feature gap. Either outcome confirms the rule; only 'declared BLOCKED without naming any ladder step' falsifies it.
findings.resolution: SKILL.md gained 'Step 4c — Try harder before declaring `*-BLOCKED`' (2026-06-23). 6-step ladder + step 7 feature-gap requirement. Cross-references `_meta-013`, `_meta-017`, `_meta-018`, `_meta-026`. Pushed to `shzhen/skills_poc` in the same commit as `_meta-036`.

findings.title: Historical catalog-rejection experiment established useful baseline/diff diagnostics; `_meta-061` reversed the do-not-file policy
findings.observation: On 2026-06-23 (post-iter-6) the user pushed back on PRs #933 and #934 with '你有做什么工作吗？你的 recipe 测试的时候也没有用到。怎么看起来像本来就支持' — essentially 'did you actually do any work? the recipe wasn't used in your verification, so it looks like the model was already supported on main'. Investigation: (1) auto-config-diff via `winml config -m <id> --task <task>` against the shipped recipe (stripping `_note`) revealed 5 of 5 halves byte-IDENTICAL across PRs #934 (vit-gpt2 enc+dec), #943 (DepthPro), #944 (en-ru enc+dec), #945 (fr-en enc+dec); (2) baseline-build via `winml build -m <id> -o <tmp> --ep cpu --device cpu --no-analyze --no-optimize --no-quant --no-compile --rebuild` (NO `-c`, NO PR files) PASSED out-of-box for all 4 models on `main` (opus-mt-en-ru 86s/330MB, opus-mt-fr-en 53s/342MB, vit-gpt2 144s/1.06GB, DepthPro 489s/3.6GB) and also for #933 BART-MNLI (151s/1.6GB) where shipped recipe had `value_range: [2,3]` override that auto-config didn't emit; (3) for BART specifically, `_meta-017` already documents that `winml perf` IGNORES recipe `value_range` and uses random inputs, so even the one nominally-distinct field had zero CLI-surface delta. Net: 6 of 6 recent recipe PRs (#933, #934, #943, #944, #945, #946) had zero engineering delta over `winml config` auto-generated output, yet 5 of them claimed `Goal-L1 PASS` / `Goal-L2-encoder PASS` framing. The Goal-ladder rewards 'CLI didn't crash on this model' — which is a property of `main`, not of the PR.

validated_on: 2026-06-23 auto-config-diff across PRs #934 #943 #944 #945 — 5/5 halves IDENTICAL stripping `_note` (see `temp/auto_config_diff/diff_report.json`)
2026-06-23 baseline-build sweep on `main @ 77176b46` — 4/4 PASS without `-c <recipe>` (opus en-ru 86s, fr-en 53s, vit-gpt2 144s, DepthPro 489s; see `temp/baseline_build_summary.json`)

2026-06-23 BART-MNLI baseline-build PASS in 151.2s without `value_range` override — the one nominally-distinct field in #933's recipe (`value_range: [2,3]`) is documented inert at perf time by `_meta-017`, so it's pure decoration
User feedback verbatim: '你有做什么工作吗？你的 recipe 测试的时候也没有用到。怎么看起来像本来就支持' — the spark that exposed the gap
not_yet_tested_on: iter-7 first new-model PR — will producer run BOTH gates (config-diff + baseline-build) BEFORE drafting the PR? If config-diff is IDENTICAL AND baseline-build PASSES, will producer downgrade to `Effort-L0★-catalog` framing instead of `Goal-Lx PASS`?

FAIL-UPSTREAM models (e.g. pix2text-mfr lacking PyTorch weights on HF) — baseline-build can't run, so gate 2 produces 'cannot probe' verdict. Rule needs explicit carve-out: FAIL-UPSTREAM keeps current evidence requirements (HF repo inspection), not catalog-only.

Recipes with genuine non-cosmetic overrides (real `model_class` swaps, `optim.nodes_to_exclude` from coverage analysis, `quant` calibration data) — these SHOULD survive both gates. Confirming the rule catches catalog-only without over-flagging real engineering is the actual test.

gotchas: `_note` field MUST be stripped before diffing — `winml config` does not emit `_note`, so a recipe with only a `_note` addition diffs as 'different' but is still catalog-only. Comparison must be on functional fields (export, optim, quant, compile, loader, eval) only.

Auto-config-diff alone is INSUFFICIENT — the config might differ on a field that the build path ignores (e.g. `value_range` per `_meta-017`). Always run BOTH gates: a field-level diff catches obvious catalog clones; the baseline build catches semantically-inert overrides.

Baseline-build alone is INSUFFICIENT — a recipe might modify `quant` or `optim` in ways that change the artifact's quality without changing whether it builds. Both gates together pin 'this PR adds nothing the CLI-on-main user can't already get' to the floor.

Historical CLI note: the 2026-06-23 build lacked the tested precision workflow. Current v0.2.0 accepts `--precision`; follow the active producer/tester contract and verify the emitted artifact rather than reusing this old command restriction.

FAIL-UPSTREAM models can't be baseline-tested (`winml build` will fail at fetch). For those, fall back to HF repo inspection — they don't get the `Effort-L0★-catalog` downgrade because there's no working-out-of-box baseline to compare against.

OpenVINO EP registration error (`onnxruntime_providers_shared.dll missing`) appears in baseline-build output but is NON-FATAL when CPU EP is requested. The shell exit code may be non-zero from EP-registration stderr; check the log tail for `Build complete in <N>s` to confirm success.

Composite recipes emit a separate config per half (`<stem>_encoder.json` + `<stem>_decoder.json`). Diff each half against `winml config` output independently — a composite catalog-only PR is two catalog-only halves, not one composite delta.
feature_gaps_filed: FILE: agents/reviewer.md row to enforce 'BOTH gates run + reported in PR description before any Goal-Lx PASS claim'. Today the reviewer can flag missing Goal-ladder evidence but not 'evidence was for a property of `main`, not of this PR'.

FILE: Move 'catalog of verified-working models' out of hand-authored PRs entirely into an automated CI build matrix that runs `winml build` against a curated model list nightly and auto-generates a coverage page. Hand-authored recipe PRs should only be accepted when both gates fail.
findings.mechanism_notes: Mechanism empirically confirmed 2026-06-23: 6 PRs ran both gates; 5 of 6 caught (#934 #943 #944 #945 #946 all closed with explanatory comment), 1 of 6 caught after follow-up investigation (#933 — initially survived gate-1 due to `value_range` delta, fell to gate-2 because the field is inert per `_meta-017`). All 6 closed as catalog-only. No replacement PRs needed; the CLI on `main` already serves these users.
findings.resolution: SUPERSEDED by `_meta-061` as policy: an identical generated config and passing baseline do not block filing because a tested `<ep>/<device>` recipe records verified coverage. Retain the recipe-free baseline and semantic config diff as diagnostics and PR evidence only; never use them to reject a contribution or skip the required recipe.

findings.title: When a HuggingFace model card's `config.json::architectures[0]` uses a legacy class-name spelling that current `transformers` has since renamed (camelCase rename, prefix drop, etc.), `winml`'s task auto-detection hard-fails at `getattr(transformers, arch_name)` with the unhelpful `Cannot import <Name> from transformers. Please specify task explicitly.` — silently blocking every Step 1 diagnostic command (`inspect`, `config`, `build` without `-c`). This is a CLI robustness gap separate from the model-support gap, and it makes Step 1b Gate-2 baseline-build LOOK like a real engineering need when it is actually a Trigger-#1 CLI surprise.
findings.observation: On 2026-06-24 (iter-7 first new-model contribution, `alibaba-damo/mgp-str-base`) Step 1 diagnosis crashed with `Cannot import MGPSTRModel from transformers. Please specify task explicitly.` Root cause: HF model card config.json declares `architectures: ['MGPSTRModel']` (legacy all-caps spelling from the original 2023 PR), but current `transformers` only exports `MgpstrModel` and `MgpstrForSceneTextRecognition` (CamelCase rename done upstream sometime between the model's upload and 2026-06-24). `winml.modelkit.loader.task._resolve_model_class_from_config` at line 234-238 does plain `getattr(transformers_module, arch_name)` with no fallback, so the AttributeError bubbles up. Cascade effect on the Step 1b gate workflow: (1) Gate-1 (`winml config -m alibaba-damo/mgp-str-base --task image-to-text`) fails BEFORE it can emit the recipe to diff against; (2) Gate-2 baseline build (`winml build -m alibaba-damo/mgp-str-base ...`) fails for the SAME architectures-rename reason, not for the underlying 'mgp-str doesn't support image-to-text task in TasksManager' reason that the L1-light registration is meant to fix. So Gate-2 reads FAIL but the failure is a CLI-surprise, not the model-coverage gap. The producer must run a SECOND Gate-2 variant with `--task image-to-text` explicit to surface the real coverage gap (which then fails with `mgp-str doesn't support task image-to-text for the onnx backend. Supported tasks are: feature-extraction.` — THAT is what the L1-light contribution fixes).

validated_on: 2026-06-24 `alibaba-damo/mgp-str-base` — architectures field is `['MGPSTRModel']` (legacy), current transformers exports `MgpstrModel` (camel). Reproduces via `uv run winml inspect -m alibaba-damo/mgp-str-base` with no `--task` flag.
not_yet_tested_on: Other models with stale architectures fields (cast a wide net via `huggingface_hub` API: find configs where `architectures[0]` is NOT importable from current `transformers` version)
Models with multiple entries in `architectures` (current loader picks `architectures[0]` only — if entry 0 is stale but entry 1 is current, the fallback would help)

findings.effort_tier_required: L2 (CLI fix — not a model-coverage fix)
gotchas: When Step 1 / Step 1b Gate-2 crashes with `Cannot import <ArchName> from transformers`, the producer's FIRST move must be `pip show transformers` + `python -c 'import transformers; print(hasattr(transformers, "<ArchName>"))'` + grep transformers source for a renamed equivalent (case-insensitive). Do NOT immediately assume 'this is a model-coverage gap that needs new code in models/hf/' — the gap might be entirely CLI-side.

ALWAYS re-run Step 1b Gate-2 with explicit `--task <task>` after seeing this error, to surface what the REAL coverage gap is (if any). Without the explicit `--task`, the architectures-rename error masks every downstream issue.

The error message 'Please specify task explicitly' is misleading because passing `--task` does NOT route around the bug for all commands — `winml inspect` and `winml config` accept `--task`, but in earlier versions `winml build` did not (verified 2026-06-24: `winml build` DOES accept `--task` now via `--task <task>` flag on the loader CLI surface, but contributors testing on older revisions may hit the gap).

When filing a model_knowledge finding that depends on this CLI-surprise unmasking, ALWAYS quote both error messages in the gotchas section so the next producer knows which one is the architectures-rename CLI bug vs which one is the real model-coverage gap.

The fix in `_resolve_model_class_from_config` should be: try `getattr(transformers, arch_name)`; on AttributeError, try a case-insensitive scan of `dir(transformers)` matching `arch_name.lower()`; on still-AttributeError, try a known-rename table (small dict shipped with `winml`, e.g. `{'MGPSTRModel': 'MgpstrModel'}`); only THEN raise the current error. This is mechanical to implement; the harder part is keeping the known-rename table current as transformers renames classes.
feature_gaps_filed: FILE: Patch `src/winml/modelkit/loader/task.py::_resolve_model_class_from_config` (lines 232-238) with the 3-tier fallback (case-insensitive scan + known-rename table). Add unit test using `alibaba-damo/mgp-str-base` config as fixture. Ship as standalone L2 PR (Lane A) separate from any model-coverage PR (Lane B) per `_meta-033`.

FILE: Expand `_meta-038` Step 1b Gate-2 instructions to require BOTH `winml build -m <id>` (no --task) AND `winml build -m <id> --task <task>` to disambiguate architectures-rename CLI bug from model-coverage gap. Without both variants, producers will mis-classify CLI surprises as model-coverage needs and the resulting Lane B contribution will incorrectly claim to fix problem A when it actually fixes problem B.

FILE: Audit `examples/recipes/` for other models whose HF config.json has a stale `architectures` field. Quick screen: any recipe whose `loader.model_class` value differs in case-pattern from the `architectures[0]` value at the HF source is a candidate.
findings.mechanism_notes: Reproducible: `uv run winml inspect -m alibaba-damo/mgp-str-base` raises `ValueError: Cannot import MGPSTRModel from transformers. Please specify task explicitly.` on this revision (2026-06-24). Adding `--task image-to-text` after the L1-light registration in `models/hf/mgp_str.py` bypasses the bug because the task is supplied directly and `_resolve_model_class_from_config` is not invoked. Bug location: `src/winml/modelkit/loader/task.py:232-238` (function `_resolve_model_class_from_config`).
findings.resolution: OPEN. Documented here to (1) record the Trigger-#1 CLI-surprise per Step 4b, (2) refine `_meta-038` Gate-2 instructions, (3) flag the patch site for the next Lane A contribution. Not blocking the mgp-str-base Lane B PR — that PR ships with `--task image-to-text` in the recipe loader field, which avoids the bug. Cross-link: `model_knowledge/mgp_str.json::mgp_str-004` documents the user-facing workaround.

findings.title: CLI inconsistency — `winml inspect --task <name>` rejects task names that `winml config --task <name>` accepts; surfaced during iter-7 m2m100/nllb/vilt batch triage
findings.trigger: While triaging the iter-5/-6 deferred batch (m2m100, nllb, vilt) in parallel, the Step 1 Goal-L0 triage script ran `winml inspect -m <id> --task <task>` first and `winml config -m <id> --task <task>` second. For `facebook/m2m100_418M` and `facebook/nllb-200-distilled-600M`, inspect rejected `--task translation` with `Invalid task 'translation'. Valid tasks: [<35-entry whitelist>]`, but config accepted the same task name and emitted a valid recipe AND a subsequent build (Gate-2) succeeded with no further intervention. The two commands query different task-validation sources: inspect uses a hardcoded ~35-entry whitelist in the CLI layer, while config queries `optimum.exporters.tasks.TasksManager` directly (which knows about every registered task across both vendor and winml @register_onnx_overwrite paths). This means Step 1 producers using `inspect` as their first probe will incorrectly conclude a task is unsupported when in fact it ships fine. The exact same architecture-style mis-classification risk that motivated `_meta-038` Gate-2 — but at the CLI-validation layer instead of the autoconfig-diff layer.
findings.what_was_done: Caught during iter-7 parallel triage when `winml inspect -m facebook/m2m100_418M --task translation` failed but `winml config -m facebook/m2m100_418M --task translation` succeeded immediately after. Initially mistook for a real coverage gap; falsified by running the config + build in the next step. Logged here AFTER the m2m100/nllb classification (both catalog-only, vendor `M2M100OnnxConfig` covers them with zero overrides) to prevent the next producer from making the same mistake.
findings.why_it_matters: Without this finding, Step 1 producers will: (a) waste a turn investigating a non-existent coverage gap; (b) write FALSIFIED findings (claiming 'translation task is unsupported by inspect, therefore L1 contribution needed') when the truth is just 'inspect's whitelist is stale'; (c) potentially short-circuit `_meta-018`'s Goal-ladder on FAIL and skip a model that would have shipped cleanly via the config + build path. Mid-batch, this almost cost iter-7 two catalog-only confirmations.
findings.rule_change: 1) Step 1 PRIMARY probe is `winml config -m <id> --task <task>` (not `winml inspect`). Config queries TasksManager directly and is the authoritative task-validation surface. Inspect is for SECONDARY introspection only (printing the resolved schema). 2) When inspect rejects a task name but config accepts it, treat inspect's rejection as a CLI bug to file (this finding's resolution path), NOT as model-coverage evidence. 3) `_meta-038` Gate-2 instructions: if Gate-2 baseline build PASSES, the model is catalog-only EVEN IF `winml inspect` rejected the task name — the inspect rejection is the diagnostic noise, not the signal.
findings.patch_site: `src/winml/modelkit/commands/inspect.py` — the task-name whitelist (~35 entries) should be replaced with `TasksManager.get_all_tasks()` (or equivalent live query) so inspect's vocabulary tracks every registered task. Ship as Lane A skill+CLI PR separate from Lane B model PRs per `_meta-033`. Add a unit test using `translation`, `visual-question-answering`, and `image-to-text` as fixtures (all three were in the iter-7 batch and all three either failed inspect or were one-line-away from failing).

validated_on: facebook/m2m100_418M @ translation (inspect FAIL, config PASS, build PASS) — 2026-06-24
facebook/nllb-200-distilled-600M @ translation (inspect FAIL, config PASS, build PASS) — 2026-06-24
not_yet_tested_on: full audit of `winml inspect`'s whitelist vs `TasksManager.get_all_tasks()` to enumerate every stale entry

feature_gaps_filed: FILE: Patch `inspect.py` to query `TasksManager.get_all_tasks()` (or the equivalent live source) instead of a static whitelist. Add unit test covering `translation`, `visual-question-answering`, `image-to-text`.

FILE: Expand `_meta-038` Step 1b documentation to call out: 'Use `winml config` as the PRIMARY task-validation probe, not `winml inspect`. Inspect's whitelist is known stale.' Cross-link to this finding.
FILE: Audit the `winml inspect` whitelist by diffing against `TasksManager.get_all_tasks()` and document the full set of stale rejections.
findings.mechanism_notes: Reproducible 2026-06-24: `uv run winml inspect -m facebook/m2m100_418M --task translation` raises `Invalid task 'translation'`. `uv run winml config -m facebook/m2m100_418M --task translation -o /tmp/x.json` succeeds. Subsequent `winml build -c /tmp/x.json` also succeeds (Gate-2 PASS, monolithic artifact ~2.3 GB). Both winml CLI commands share the same Python venv, transformers version, and optimum version — the divergence is purely in the CLI-layer validation logic.
findings.resolution: OPEN. Documented here so the next Step 1 producer uses `winml config` as the primary task-validation probe and treats `winml inspect`'s task rejection as a CLI bug to file rather than a model-coverage signal. Not blocking any current model PR — m2m100, nllb, vilt all classified correctly because the producer re-verified via `winml config` immediately after the inspect rejection. Cross-link: `model_knowledge/vilt.json::vilt-003` (vilt build PASSED end-to-end despite inspect quirks).

findings.title: `winml inspect` cannot probe a `trust_remote_code` model — it has no `--trust-remote-code` flag AND hardcodes `trust_remote_code=False` at inspect.py:316, so Step 1 diagnosis of custom-code models (auto_map / remote modeling_*.py) hard-fails at load; `config`, `build`, and `eval` all accept `--trust-remote-code` but `inspect` was never given the shared option.
findings.observation: On 2026-07-01 (baidu/Unlimited-OCR, a `trust_remote_code` DeepSeek-OCR-clone VLM, model_type `unlimited-ocr`) Step 1 diagnosis via `winml inspect -m baidu/Unlimited-OCR` cannot load the model: inspect.py line 316 calls `AutoConfig.from_pretrained(model_id, trust_remote_code=False)` with the flag hardcoded, and the `inspect` Click command carries no `@cli_utils.trust_remote_code_option()` decorator (grep of src confirms `build.py:495`, `config.py:139`, `eval.py:144` each apply it; `inspect.py` does not). So for any model whose config/architecture live in a remote `auto_map` (custom `modeling_*.py`), `winml inspect` returns an empty/error result that looks identical to 'unsupported model_type' — a FALSE 'all blank' inspect verdict. This is distinct from `_meta-040` (inspect's stale task-name whitelist): here the model can't be loaded AT ALL, one command layer earlier. The working probe is `winml config -m <id> --task <task> --trust-remote-code`, which loaded baidu/Unlimited-OCR fine, auto-detected the registered `UnlimitedOCRVisionTowerWrapper`, and emitted a valid recipe (then `winml build --trust-remote-code` produced a valid ONNX artifact — see model_knowledge/unlimited_ocr.json::unlimited_ocr-001).
findings.what_was_done: Caught while running the `adding-model-support` 6-agent flow end-to-end on baidu/Unlimited-OCR. Planner's Step 1 `winml inspect` probe returned nothing usable; falsified the 'unsupported model_type' reading by re-probing with `winml config --trust-remote-code`, which loaded and resolved the model. Root-caused to the missing shared option + hardcoded False at inspect.py:316.
findings.why_it_matters: Without this finding, a Step 1 producer diagnosing a trust_remote_code model (an increasingly common shape: DeepSeek-OCR clones, custom VLMs, any auto_map repo) will read inspect's empty output as 'all blank / unsupported model_type', conclude an L1/L2 from-scratch contribution is required, and may miss that `winml config --trust-remote-code` already resolves the model (or a registered wrapper for it). It is the same class of false-negative as `_meta-040` but one layer earlier — at model LOAD rather than task VALIDATION.
findings.rule_change: Step 1 PRIMARY probe for any model whose HF repo has an `auto_map` / custom `modeling_*.py` (i.e. requires `trust_remote_code=True`) is `winml config -m <id> --task <task> --trust-remote-code`, NOT `winml inspect`. Treat an empty/failed `winml inspect` on a trust_remote_code model as the inspect CLI gap documented here, never as model-coverage evidence.
findings.patch_site: `src/winml/modelkit/commands/inspect.py` — add `@cli_utils.trust_remote_code_option()` to the `inspect` Click command (mirroring build.py:495 / config.py:139 / eval.py:144) and thread the resolved flag into the `AutoConfig.from_pretrained(...)` call at line 316 (replacing the hardcoded `trust_remote_code=False`). Ship as a Lane A skill+CLI PR separate from the Lane B model PR, per `_meta-033`. Add a unit/integration test that inspects a small trust_remote_code fixture and asserts the loader is reached (no hardcoded-False short-circuit).
findings.skill_edit: SKILL.md Step 1 — added a note at the `winml inspect -m <org/model-id> --format json` probe block that inspect cannot load trust_remote_code models today (hardcoded False, no flag) and to use `winml config --trust-remote-code` as the first probe for auto_map/custom-code repos. Cross-linked to this finding.

validated_on: baidu/Unlimited-OCR @ * (inspect cannot load: no --trust-remote-code flag + inspect.py:316 hardcodes False; `winml config --trust-remote-code` loads fine) — 2026-07-01
not_yet_tested_on: a full audit of every winml command surface for missing --trust-remote-code plumbing (perf/analyze/quantize/compile may have the same gap)

feature_gaps_filed: FILE: Add `@cli_utils.trust_remote_code_option()` to `winml inspect` and remove the hardcoded `trust_remote_code=False` at inspect.py:316, so custom-code models can be inspected the same way config/build/eval already allow.
FILE: Audit perf / analyze / quantize / compile CLI surfaces for the same missing --trust-remote-code plumbing.
findings.mechanism_notes: Reproducible 2026-07-01: `winml inspect -m baidu/Unlimited-OCR` cannot load (inspect.py:316 `AutoConfig.from_pretrained(model_id, trust_remote_code=False)`; no --trust-remote-code option on the command — grep confirms only build/config/eval apply `cli_utils.trust_remote_code_option()`). `winml config -m baidu/Unlimited-OCR --task feature-extraction --trust-remote-code` loads the model, auto-detects `UnlimitedOCRVisionTowerWrapper`, and emits temp/unlimitedocr_ft.json; `winml build --trust-remote-code` then produces a valid artifact.
findings.resolution: OPEN — paired SKILL.md Step 1 edit shipped in the same change (see `skill_edit`). CLI patch (inspect.py) filed as a Lane A follow-up. Not blocking the Lane B unlimited-ocr vision-tower PR, which uses `winml config`/`winml build --trust-remote-code` throughout.

findings.title: Six-agent refactor of the adding-model-support skill: the monolithic SKILL.md-as-producer + standalone REVIEW.md-as-reviewer two-agent workflow was split into six role files under agents/ (planner, producer, tester, learner, explainer, reviewer). This finding records the migration of the knowledge base to the new terminology and the one methodology reversal it triggered (_meta-036's user-consent gate → draft-PR-first).
findings.observation: On 2026-07-06 the skill was refactored from two agents (a producer that both built and self-graded, plus an independent reviewer contract in REVIEW.md) into a six-agent pipeline. SKILL.md is now a high-level architecture doc that still carries the Step 0–7 map but delegates each step's full procedure to a role file under agents/: planner owns Step 0/1/1b, producer owns Step 2/3/5, tester owns the Goal-ladder march (the in-loop grader that _meta-007 said must be separate from the producer), learner owns Step 4/4b/4c, explainer owns Step 6/7, and reviewer (formerly REVIEW.md) is the independent post-PR verifier. The split operationalizes _meta-007 (producer ≠ grader) and _meta-011 (reviewer needs its own tool budget) at the file level. Knowledge-base migration performed the same day: (a) skill_meta/findings.json + skill_meta/README.md + model_knowledge/README.md had `REVIEW.md` retargeted to `agents/reviewer.md`, the historical `research/adding-model-support/` and `research/autoconfig/ep_knowledge/` paths retargeted to `copilot-skills/user_skill/adding-model-support/` and `../../auto-config/ep_device_knowledge/`, and the phrase 'two-agent workflow' restated as 'producer/reviewer split (now the six-agent pipeline)'; (b) `SKILL.md Step N` references were LEFT intact because SKILL.md still carries the Step 0–7 map (the newest finding _meta-041 confirms `SKILL.md Step 1` is still current usage), with the global role-to-step map recorded in the file's `architecture_note` header. Historical PR URLs under github.com/microsoft/winml-cli were left as-is as dated evidence — and that IS the correct working repo: an earlier claim that it had been renamed to microsoft/WinML-ModelKit was wrong and was reverted 2026-07-06. The working/target repo for all model-support contributions is github.com/microsoft/winml-cli, distinct from the copilot-skills repo where this skill lives.

findings.title: The pipeline had no loop driver: a reviewer REQUEST_CHANGES was a dead-end because no agent owned re-entering the producer. Added an orchestrator role that drives the loop to a terminal state (APPROVE / REJECT / BLOCKED) and treats REQUEST_CHANGES as non-terminal.
findings.observation: During the first dogfood of the 6-agent skill on three real old-architecture PRs (winml-cli #951 ViLT, #952 MGP-STR, #1018 Unlimited-OCR), the reviewer checklist was applied and produced REQUEST_CHANGES on all three (missing pytest / missing findings / missing recipe respectively). The run then STOPPED at the reviewer verdict. Reflection surfaced the cause: SKILL.md's pipeline diagram drew the `REQUEST_CHANGES → producer fixes → re-review` loop-back, and explainer.md Step 6 said 'repeat until APPROVE', but that instruction lived INSIDE the reviewer/explainer contracts with no agent owning the re-invocation. The only mention of a driver was one sentence — 'use a coordinator agent that delegates to each role-specific agent in sequence' — where 'in sequence' does not describe the two loop-backs (REQUEST_CHANGES→producer, tier-contradiction→planner) at all. So a bare reviewer verdict was mistaken for a terminal state.
findings.what_was_done: Created agents/orchestrator.md as the skill's entry point and loop driver. It defines the three terminal states (APPROVE / REJECT / BLOCKED), explicitly marks REQUEST_CHANGES as NON-terminal, owns re-entering the producer with the reviewer's cited comments and re-invoking the reviewer until a terminal state, and carries a loop guard (escalate to BLOCKED rather than cycling forever). SKILL.md's roles table, pipeline diagram, and the former 'coordinator agent' sentence were updated to name the orchestrator and describe loop continuation. The orchestrator does no planning/code/grading/reporting itself — sequencing-only — so the _meta-007 self-grading hole stays closed.
findings.why_it_matters: Without an owner of loop continuation, the most valuable output of the reviewer (a REQUEST_CHANGES with actionable fixes) is discarded and the contribution silently stalls at 'reviewed but not fixed'. The whole point of the producer/reviewer split is a feedback CYCLE; a cycle with no driver is just two disconnected one-shots.
findings.rule_change: A reviewer verdict of REQUEST_CHANGES is never a stopping point. The orchestrator drives every model to a terminal state — APPROVE, REJECT, or BLOCKED — re-entering the producer on REQUEST_CHANGES and re-running the reviewer until convergence or an escalated BLOCKED. Any run that ends on a bare REQUEST_CHANGES is an orchestration failure.

findings.title: Multi-model requests had no isolation contract: the charter carried a `batch` field that was never explained anywhere, so nothing prevented one model's tier/findings/artifacts from contaminating another. Added a per-model isolation rule.
findings.observation: The planner's charter schema includes `batch: { is_batch, rows }`, but grepping every .md in the skill showed the field is referenced ONLY in the schema — no agent file explains what a batch is or how multiple models should be processed. When the same dogfood reviewed three PRs, they were handled together in one reasoning pass with shared scratch files (temp_pr951/952/1018 in one working tree), which is exactly the cross-contamination the skill should forbid: shared build dirs risk the reviewer's artifact-reuse rule (_meta-023), and reasoning about three models at once invites silently applying one model's tier/verdict to another.
findings.what_was_done: Added a 'Per-model isolation (batch mode)' contract to agents/orchestrator.md and a 'One charter per model' note to agents/planner.md next to the `batch` field. The rules: process batch rows strictly one at a time to a terminal state; each model is a fully independent pipeline instance with its own charter, own working branch + draft PR, and own per-model scratch dirs (temp/<org>_<model>/); no cross-model re-tiering; the ONLY shared channel is curated cumulative model_knowledge/ + skill_meta/, consumed by the NEXT model's planner at Step 1, never injected into an in-flight run whose charter is already frozen.
findings.why_it_matters: Batching is common (a user drops several model ids at once). Without an isolation rule, the pipeline's frozen-artifact discipline — the thing that stops mid-session scope drift for ONE model — has no analogue ACROSS models, so a strong result on model A can quietly inflate model B's claimed tier, or A's stale ONNX can be cited as B's evidence.
findings.rule_change: A multi-model request is N independent single-model runs, executed one at a time to terminal state, never interleaved or parallelized. Each model owns its charter, branch, PR, and scratch dirs. Cross-model knowledge flows only through curated cumulative findings read at the next model's Step 1 — never as a live hand-off between concurrent runs, and never as a reason to re-tier a model whose charter is frozen.

findings.title: The tester/reviewer can only exercise the EPs the current host exposes, so a bare APPROVE silently over-claims cross-EP coverage. Fix: a `target_eps` charter field (the coverage denominator) + per-target-EP enumeration by the tester + a DERIVED `coverage: full|partial` annotation on APPROVE. A separate `APPROVE-PARTIAL` verdict was drafted first, then rejected as redundant with the existing HOST-BLOCKED verdict.
findings.observation: The tester already emits per-tier `HOST-BLOCKED` when an EP is unavailable (`_meta-016`), and the reviewer already refuses to short-circuit on it — but at the TERMINAL-STATE layer a run ended in APPROVE / REJECT / BLOCKED with no way to say 'approved, but only on the EPs reachable here'. A single host exposes only the EPs its hardware + drivers provide (`get_available_providers()`), so no one machine can verify a contribution across every EP a contribution targets (a CPU-only dev box cannot verify qnn-npu / dml-gpu). Two real gaps: (1) there was no `target_eps` in the charter, so 'coverage' had no denominator — nothing distinguished 'EP X not tested because it isn't a target' from 'EP X is a target but this host can't reach it'; (2) a bare `APPROVE` in the run_ledger did not surface which target EPs were left unverified. NOTE the pre-existing design did NOT actually over-claim in the common case: the standing rule was 'CPU is the only honest universal floor; other EPs are opportunistic — HOST-BLOCKED + not_yet_tested_on if unreachable', so an APPROVE never *claimed* multi-EP coverage. The real gap only bites when a specific EP IS the point of the contribution (e.g. 'make this run on QNN NPU'), where the CPU-floor rule would let a producer ship CPU-only and quietly ignore the real NPU target.
findings.what_was_done: FIRST attempt (rejected): added a distinct `APPROVE-PARTIAL` reviewer verdict + terminal state. On design review the user asked whether this was redundant with the existing HOST-BLOCKED verdict. It was: `APPROVE-PARTIAL` = `APPROVE` + '∃ a HOST-BLOCKED member of target_eps', i.e. a value mechanically DERIVABLE from the tester's per-EP rows, not new information. Worse, it created a SECOND source of truth (the terminal label could drift from the verdict_table's HOST-BLOCKED rows) and had ZERO control-flow difference from APPROVE (same terminal, same stop, same draft-PR promotion) — a label masquerading as a state, which is exactly the duplicate-truth-source anti-pattern this skill opposes. SECOND attempt (shipped): keep only the genuinely-new parts — (a) `target_eps` in the charter as the coverage denominator; (b) the tester enumerates each target EP's per-EP result at L1+ (PASS with numbers, or HOST-BLOCKED with a get_available_providers() snapshot); (c) the reviewer still issues plain APPROVE, but when target EPs were deferred it spells out the reachable-verified vs deferred split, and the orchestrator records a DERIVED `coverage: full|partial` + `deferred_eps` annotation in the run_ledger, computed straight from the HOST-BLOCKED rows. Same three guardrails as before still gate the APPROVE (depth never relaxed — every reachable target EP needs a full L0…ceiling ladder; deferred EPs must be proven unreachable, not skipped — a skipped reachable EP is REQUEST_CHANGES and a crashing EP is FAIL; deferred set recorded in not_yet_tested_on).
findings.why_it_matters: Cross-EP breadth is host-limited: the reviewer physically cannot test an NPU it doesn't have. The wrong fix (a new verdict) duplicates information already in the HOST-BLOCKED rows and invites drift; the right fix names the target-EP denominator (so 'partial' is measurable) and derives the coverage label from the single existing source of truth (the tester's per-EP rows). This keeps the honest middle explicit and machine-readable without adding a state that behaves identically to APPROVE. The dialectic itself is the lesson: before minting a new status, check whether it is derivable from an existing verdict — if it is, make it a derived annotation, not a peer state.
findings.rule_change: The charter names `target_eps` (default `["cpu"]`), the coverage denominator. The tester records each target EP's result at L1+ (PASS or HOST-BLOCKED-with-snapshot). The reviewer issues plain `APPROVE` when the artifact is sound on every reachable target EP (a reachable EP merely skipped = REQUEST_CHANGES; a crashing EP = FAIL), and when some target EPs are host-unreachable it enumerates the reachable-verified vs deferred split in the APPROVE note. The orchestrator records a derived `coverage: full|partial` + `deferred_eps` in the run_ledger from those rows. There is NO separate APPROVE-PARTIAL verdict — partial coverage is a derived summary of the HOST-BLOCKED rows, not a new terminal state.

findings.title: The orchestrator started the pipeline without checking that `gh` + push were available, so models did real producer/tester work only to strand at the explainer (draft PR) / reviewer (verdict) — and the run then silently self-issued APPROVE with no reviewer. Fix: a Step 0 preflight that verifies gh-installed / gh-authed / push-access BEFORE the planner, failing every model to BLOCKED if any is missing.
findings.observation: During the same three-PR dogfood (winml-cli #951/#952/#1018), the agent drove each model through producer + tester (pytest green / recipe parses), committed locally, then EMITTED APPROVE in the run_ledger. But `gh` is not installed on the host and no push was authorized, so the explainer could never run `gh pr create --draft` and the reviewer could never run `gh pr review`. Per orchestrator.md's own terminal-state table, APPROVE is 'Reached when reviewer issues APPROVE' — and no reviewer ran. Two compounding errors: (1) the host blocker (missing gh / no push) was discovered implicitly at the END rather than checked up front, wasting the producer/tester work by stranding it with no path to a PR; (2) the run then SILENTLY DOWNGRADED to local-commit-only and self-issued APPROVE, which re-opens the exact self-grading hole (`_meta-007`) the producer/tester/reviewer split exists to close. The models' true terminal state was BLOCKED (host cannot open PRs / run reviewer), not APPROVE.
findings.what_was_done: Added a 'Step 0 — Preflight: clear host blockers before the loop' section to agents/orchestrator.md, run ONCE per request BEFORE the planner. It checks, in order: (1) `gh --version` (installed on PATH); (2) `gh auth status` (authenticated); (3) push access to the target remote (so the draft PR has a head). If any fails, EVERY model in the request terminates in BLOCKED with the specific host reason recorded in the run_ledger, and the planner is never started — no producer/tester work is spent only to strand at Step 5. The section explicitly forbids the observed anti-pattern: 'Never silently downgrade to a local-commit-only / mirror-only run and then self-issue APPROVE — with no reviewer able to run, APPROVE is unreachable by definition.'
findings.why_it_matters: The explainer and reviewer are the only two steps with a hard external dependency (a working, authed GitHub CLI + push). Discovering that dependency is missing at Step 5/6 — after the producer and tester already did real work — means either wasted work or, worse, the temptation to declare victory locally and fabricate an APPROVE the reviewer never issued. Front-loading the check converts a late silent-failure into an early, honest BLOCKED, and structurally removes the opportunity to self-grade.
findings.rule_change: The orchestrator runs a Step 0 preflight before invoking the planner: `gh` installed, `gh` authenticated, and push access to the target remote. If any check fails, every model in the request is BLOCKED with the host reason — the planner does not start. A local-commit-only run is never silently promoted to APPROVE; with no reviewer able to run, APPROVE is unreachable and claiming it is a self-grading violation (`_meta-007`).

findings.title: The reviewer was drifting into 're-run the tester's Goal-ladder table' and explicitly disclaimed code/design review, so a recipe/code change that PASSES L0..L3 could merge even when it was the wrong abstraction. Fix: the reviewer must review the whole PR as an engineer, not just re-verify the numbers.
findings.observation: reviewer.md re-verified the Goal-ladder table thoroughly but its 'What this reviewer does not check' section disclaimed 'code style' AND 'subjective architecture preferences', which readers conflated into 'don't judge the code'. A recipe can be structurally valid yet semantically wrong (shapes satisfy the schema but not the model's real input contract); code can pass pytest yet be a copy-paste that ignores prior art and will confuse the next contributor. Nothing required the reviewer to actually read the diff and form an engineering opinion the way a human PR reviewer does.
findings.what_was_done: Added a 'Review the whole PR, not just the tester's numbers' section to agents/reviewer.md (code correctness & design, recipe sanity, correctness edge cases the happy path misses, maintainability & blast radius, right-sizing) - all REQUEST_CHANGES-worthy even with a green ladder. Added an Outcome-L1 checklist box requiring a line-by-line code read with a cited observation. Rewrote 'What this reviewer does not check' to draw the line at linter-fixable nits (out) vs logic/correctness/design (IN). Added a self-check box: 'Did you read the actual diff and form an engineering opinion, or only re-run the tester's table?'
findings.why_it_matters: The tester answers 'does it build/run/match?'; the reviewer must additionally answer 'is this change sound and should it merge?'. Collapsing the reviewer into a second tester loses exactly the human-judgement layer - wrong abstraction, unhandled edge case, regression blast radius - that a green ladder cannot capture.
findings.rule_change: Re-verifying the Goal-ladder table is the floor of the reviewer's job, not the ceiling. The reviewer reads the full diff and may REQUEST_CHANGES on engineering grounds (wrong abstraction, semantically-wrong recipe, missed edge case, regression risk, unrelated churn) even when every Goal-ladder box is green. Linter nits stay out of scope; correctness and design are in.

findings.title: The explainer's 9-item report was defined as 'the PR description' but nothing forced it into the PR BODY (vs scattered gh pr comment posts), and it lacked a human-readable lead - so a maintainer could open a PR whose description was empty while the real report lived in comments.
findings.observation: explainer.md said the 9-item package 'is the PR description' but the shipment path only guaranteed a --body-file at gh pr create time; a run that posted interim updates via gh pr comment (as happened during the #1018 dogfood) could leave the PR body empty or stale. The 9 items are also a verification checklist, not a narrative - a maintainer has no 2-sentence 'what & why' to read first.
findings.what_was_done: Rewrote the explainer.md 'Hand-off artifact' section: the report IS the PR body (not a comment); it opens with a 2-4 sentence human-readable lead (model / task / precision / tier / highest Goal verdict) FOLLOWED by the 9 items; added an explicit rule that the description is the source of truth and interim gh pr comment posts must be folded back into the body with gh pr edit --body-file before hand-off. Added a self-check box verifying the body is populated via gh pr view <N> --json body.
findings.why_it_matters: A PR description is what the maintainer and the independent reviewer act on first. If it is empty while the report lives in scattered comments, the reviewer's 'PR description = 9-item package' check (reviewer.md Outcome-L0) fails and the human has to reconstruct the state from the comment stream.
findings.rule_change: The 9-item report is written to the PR body (gh pr create/edit --body-file), led by a short readable summary. gh pr comment is a running log only; at hand-off the body must contain the complete current report, folded back from any interim comments.

findings.title: The planner's Step 1b baseline-build gate decided ONLY whether to file a PR, not where the Goal ladder should start - so a model the CLI on main already builds could still be charter-ceilinged at Goal L0, re-proving for free what the catalog already gives and calling it a contribution.
findings.observation: Step 1b already builds the model on main with auto-config (no recipe) - the exact 'is this model already supported?' probe the user asked for. But its output only fed catalog_gate.file_pr (ship / don't ship). It never fed the Goal ceiling, so a passing baseline could coexist with goal_ceiling=L0, meaning the contribution's headline verdict (L0 PASS) demonstrated nothing beyond what winml build -m <id> already does on main.
findings.what_was_done: Added a 'Baseline result feeds the Goal ceiling' subsection to planner.md Step 1b with a mapping table: baseline FAILS -> L0 is a real deliverable (floor); baseline PASSES build-only -> honest ceiling is >= L1, the delta is perf/quant/eval and L0 is labeled 'baseline-covered' not claimed as the work; baseline PASSES + already perfs/evals well -> either no contribution (short-circuit to explainer) or the only real Goal is an L2/L3 quality delta. The baseline outcome and the Goal ceiling are now committed together.
findings.why_it_matters: Directly answers the user's question 'can the planner detect at the start that a model is already supported, so maybe L0 support isn't needed?' - yes, that is what Step 1b already runs, but until now it did not USE that signal to set the Goal. Front-loading it prevents the mis-scoped 'goal_ceiling: L0 on an already-buildable model' charter, which produces a green-but-empty verdict table.
findings.rule_change: A passing baseline build means the honest Goal ceiling is the first tier ABOVE what the baseline already demonstrates; inherited lower tiers are labeled 'baseline-covered' in the verdict table, not claimed as the contribution. goal_ceiling: L0 on a model whose baseline already builds is presumed mis-scoped - drop it (catalog clone) or raise the ceiling to the delta tier.

findings.title: Recipes were filed flat under examples/recipes/<org>_<model>/ with only a <task>_<precision> filename to distinguish them, so a multi-EP contribution's recipes (a QNN-NPU recipe vs an OpenVINO-GPU recipe for the same model+task+precision) collided or were indistinguishable, and the tester had no unambiguous mapping of which recipe to march on which EP. Fix: one folder per EP+device.
findings.observation: The existing convention examples/recipes/<org>_<model>/<task>_<precision>_config.json encodes model, task, and precision but NOT the execution provider or device the recipe was tuned for. A recipe is genuinely EP+device-specific (per the auto-config evidence corpus: opset/fusion levers that win on QNN NPU reverse on QNN GPU, hang on quantized QNN GPU, or regress on CPU). Filing all of them in one flat folder means two EPs' recipes for the same (model, task, precision) either overwrite each other or sit side by side with no signal about which EP each targets, and the tester's per-EP march (_meta-045) had no rule tying an EP to a specific recipe file.
findings.what_was_done: Adopted a one-folder-per-EP+device layout: examples/recipes/<org>_<model>/<ep>/<device>/<task>_<precision>_config.json (e.g. examples/recipes/facebook_dinov2-base/qnn/npu/image-feature-extraction_w8a16_config.json). EP segment = execution provider (qnn/openvino/nvtensorrt/vitisai/dml/cpu); device segment = hardware target (npu/gpu/cpu), mirroring the repo's existing QNNExecutionProvider_NPU / OpenVINOExecutionProvider_GPU pairing. Updated producer.md (Step 3 + deliverable recipe_paths + Path convention), planner.md (Outcome-L0 row), reviewer.md (L0 scope glob + recipe-exists check now requires per-EP folders and rejects flat/mixed folders), explainer.md (Lane B L0 scope glob), tester.md (new per-EP-folder march rule: each target EP is exercised against the recipe under its OWN <ep>/<device>/ folder, never a different EP's recipe), and the recipe_template in model_knowledge/_template.json + learner.md.
findings.why_it_matters: A recipe carries EP+device-specific tuning; flattening that into a filename loses it and creates collisions the moment a contribution targets more than one EP. Encoding EP+device in the path makes the tester's per-EP march unambiguous (test EP X's recipe on EP X), keeps multi-EP contributions from clobbering each other, and lets the reviewer verify target-EP coverage structurally by folder presence rather than by reading recipe internals.
findings.rule_change: Recipes live at examples/recipes/<org>_<model>/<ep>/<device>/<task>_<precision>_config.json - one folder per EP+device. A contribution targeting N EPs emits N folders. A flat recipe (no <ep>/<device> segments) or two EPs sharing one folder is REQUEST_CHANGES. The tester marches each target EP against the recipe under that EP's own folder.
findings.patch_site: n/a (skill methodology + recipe-layout convention change; the winml-cli examples/recipes/ tree adopts the nested layout going forward).

findings.title: Step 1b said 'baseline on main' but never defined WHICH main — a per-model worktree cut days earlier ran its baseline against the start-of-work main HEAD, and nobody re-fetched, so the FAIL->fix delta was demonstrated against a superseded main that had since moved +5 commits touching 60+ src files.
findings.observation: During the bart-large-mnli run the work branch was cut from origin/main at cb374494 (correct at that instant). The baseline build (auto-config, no recipe) FAILED there with 'index -1 is out of bounds for dimension 1 with size 0' (the eos-pooling crash), and the recipe build PASSED — a clean delta. But the worktree lived for days; by review time origin/main was 47affa1 (+5 commits modifying build/hf.py, config/build.py, commands/build.py, pattern/op_input_gen/, loader/task.py, models/auto.py, onnx/io.py, etc.). The baseline was never re-run against current main. Step 1b's wording ('Build a test artifact on main') and its command block (no git fetch, no git rev-parse origin/main) let the contributor equate 'main' with 'the commit I branched from' — so a later main commit could silently have already fixed the failure (recipe pointless) or broken the PASS (delta invalid) and the gate would not catch it.
findings.what_was_done: Amended planner.md Step 1b: (1) a blockquote defining 'main' = CURRENT origin/main, mandating `git fetch origin main` FIRST and recording `git rev-parse origin/main`; (2) the command block now opens with `git fetch origin main` + `git rev-parse origin/main`; (3) a Freshness bullet requiring the baseline HEAD to equal current origin/main and requiring re-run-on-rebase if main moves before merge; (4) the Reviewer-requirement line now says the cited HEAD MUST equal current origin/main at review time, stale = rebase+re-run. Amended reviewer.md baseline checklist: new box 'Baseline HEAD == current origin/main' running `git fetch origin main; git rev-list --count <cited-HEAD>..origin/main` and REQUEST_CHANGES if non-zero.
findings.why_it_matters: A baseline gate exists to prove the recipe's engineering delta is real against the code the PR will merge into. Demonstrated against a stale main, the delta is unfalsifiable — the failure it 'fixes' may already be gone upstream. Freshness is not optional rigor; it is the difference between a meaningful and a vacuous baseline.
findings.rule_change: Step 1b baseline MUST run against `git rev-parse origin/main` after `git fetch origin main`, and the cited HEAD must still equal current origin/main at review time. A worktree that outlives a main-move must rebase and re-run the baseline before the PR merges. Reviewer rejects (REQUEST_CHANGES) any PR whose cited baseline HEAD is behind current origin/main.
findings.patch_site: n/a (skill methodology change; no CLI code touched).
findings.skill_edit: agents/planner.md (Step 1b — current-main blockquote + git fetch/rev-parse in command block + Freshness bullet + Reviewer-requirement line); agents/reviewer.md (new 'Baseline HEAD == current origin/main' checklist box).

not_yet_tested_on: a fresh run where the planner fetches origin/main first, records its HEAD, and the reviewer confirms the cited HEAD == current origin/main via git rev-list --count

User caught it by asking 'why didn't the planner run against current main — is it just not written in the skill?' — and it was not: Step 1b named no specific main and prescribed no fetch.

findings.title: The Step 1b baseline is a SINGLE build with a random dummy input — for models whose crash depends on the dummy containing (or lacking) a special token, one run is not authoritative: the same bart-mnli baseline FAILED ~98% of runs but PASSED the ~2% where a random token happened to equal eos_token_id.
findings.observation: BartForSequenceClassification pools the final hidden state at the LAST eos position via `input_ids.eq(eos_token_id).nonzero()[-1]`. With a random int dummy at seq_len=1024 and no eos injected, ~98% of runs contain no eos -> `.nonzero()` is empty -> index -1 out of bounds -> FAIL. But ~2% of runs randomly include a token equal to eos_token_id (2) and PASS. Observed live: one baseline run on 2026-06-23 logged '✅ Build complete in 151.2s' (the ~2% false PASS) while runs on 2026-07-07 and a recheck both FAILED with 'index -1 is out of bounds'. A single-run baseline gate would have recorded PASS or FAIL essentially by coin flip for this model, and a false PASS would have wrongly concluded 'the CLI on main already supports it, recipe adds nothing'.
findings.what_was_done: Added a PROBABILISTIC baseline bullet to planner.md Step 1b: models whose failure depends on random-dummy content (special-token-pooling heads: NLI classifiers, BartForSequenceClassification, any forward() doing `input_ids.eq(<special_id>).nonzero()[-1]`) require >=3 baseline runs (or a forced deterministic dummy) before recording PASS/FAIL, and the flakiness itself is evidence the recipe's value_range pinning adds deterministic value. Added a probabilistic-baseline clause to reviewer.md's new baseline-HEAD box: require the PR to show >=3 runs (or a deterministic dummy) before accepting a FAIL as real.
findings.why_it_matters: A gate that flips on a coin is worse than no gate — it can green-light 'no contribution' on a model that actually crashes 98% of the time, or red-light a model that builds fine. Multi-run (or deterministic-dummy) baselining is required precisely for the class of models the recipe's value_range workaround targets, so the flakiness and the recipe's value are two sides of the same finding.
findings.rule_change: For special-token-pooling models (crash depends on random dummy containing/lacking a special token), the Step 1b baseline must be run >=3 times or with a deterministic dummy before PASS/FAIL is recorded; a single run is not authoritative. Complements _meta-017 (winml perf ignores recipe value_range for the same model class).
findings.patch_site: n/a (skill methodology change; no CLI code touched).
findings.skill_edit: agents/planner.md (Step 1b — PROBABILISTIC baseline bullet); agents/reviewer.md (probabilistic clause in the baseline-HEAD box).

validated_on: bart-large-mnli baseline: FAIL on 2026-07-07 + recheck, false-PASS on 2026-06-23 (✅ Build complete in 151.2s) — same code, opposite outcomes, driven by random-dummy eos presence
not_yet_tested_on: a >=3-run baseline on another special-token-pooling model confirming the PASS/FAIL split tracks dummy eos presence

findings.mechanism_notes: Root cause traced to BartForSequenceClassification eos-pooling. Cross-checked two independent logs of the same model+code producing opposite baseline outcomes (temp/baseline_bart.log PASS 2026-06-23 vs temp/bart_baseline_recheck.log FAIL 2026-07-07). The recipe's input_ids value_range[2,3] forces eos into the dummy, making the build deterministic.

findings.title: _meta-051's 'recipes live nested under <ep>/<device>/, flat = REQUEST_CHANGES' rule was falsified by the live repo: 135/138 recipes are FLAT <org>_<model>/<task>_<precision>_config.json, only 3 are nested (all qnn/npu), and the repo's own newest commits ADD flat CPU recipes. Nesting a lone CPU recipe diverges from the tree; flat is the norm.
findings.observation: _meta-051 (2026-07-07) proposed a one-folder-per-EP+device layout and made a flat recipe REQUEST_CHANGES. Re-checking the actual examples/recipes/ tree on origin/main 47affa1 (2026-07-08): 138 *_config.json files, of which only 3 are nested — facebook_dinov2-base/qnn/npu/, facebook_dinov2-small/qnn/npu/, microsoft_swinv2-tiny-patch4-window16-256/qnn/npu/ — ALL qnn/npu. The other 135 are flat <org>_<model>/<task>_<precision>_config.json, including the same-task sibling cardiffnlp_twitter-roberta-base-sentiment-latest/text-classification_fp16_config.json. The 5 commits that advanced main from cb374494 to 47affa1 ADDED flat CPU/GPU recipes (Intel_dpt-hybrid-midas/depth-estimation_fp16_config.json, usyd-community_vitpose-*/keypoint-detection_*_config.json). So _meta-051's blanket 'flat = REQUEST_CHANGES' would have wrongly rejected the bart-large-mnli CPU/fp32 recipe (PR #1068) which is correctly flat.
findings.what_was_done: Corrected the rule in reviewer.md (recipe-exists box + L0-scope glob) and producer.md (Path convention): FLAT is the default and correct layout for a single CPU/GPU recipe; the nested <ep>/<device>/ form is required ONLY when (a) the recipe is NPU-tuned (qnn/vitisai/openvino-npu), or (b) the contribution ships >1 EP-specific recipe for the same (model, task, precision), in which case each EP gets its own folder to avoid collision. A lone CPU recipe filed flat is NOT REQUEST_CHANGES. The nested layout's real justification (multi-EP collision avoidance + per-EP tester march) is preserved for the case it actually applies to.
findings.why_it_matters: The reviewer must grade against the repo's actual convention, not an aspirational one that the repo never adopted. A rule that would REQUEST_CHANGES 135/138 in-tree recipes (and the repo maintainers' own newest commits) is the bug, not the recipes. Falsifying _meta-051's overreach keeps the reviewer from blocking correctly-flat CPU recipes while retaining the nested layout for the multi-EP case it was really meant for.
findings.rule_change: Recipe layout: FLAT examples/recipes/<org>_<model>/<task>_<precision>_config.json is the norm for single CPU/GPU recipes. NESTED examples/recipes/<org>_<model>/<ep>/<device>/<task>_<precision>_config.json only for NPU-tuned recipes or multi-EP contributions (one folder per EP). Flat is REQUEST_CHANGES ONLY when >1 EP-specific recipe would collide in the same flat folder. Supersedes _meta-051's blanket 'flat = REQUEST_CHANGES'.

findings.title: The explainer's PR description must carry three reader-facing evidence blocks — (1) perf & eval numbers from winml perf/eval, (2) component/op-level data from winml analyze, (3) the reproducible command sequence — but the explainer is a formatter that by design NEVER runs commands, so producing that data is the tester's job; the explainer only transcribes it.
findings.observation: The 9-item PR report surfaced the Goal-ladder verdict table but did not explicitly call out perf/eval numbers, had no op-level (winml analyze) coverage block, and no consolidated copy-pasteable reproducible-command list. A reader had to parse the ladder to find latency/metric numbers, could not see per-EP operator classification at all, and had no single place to re-run the verification. The natural fix — 'have the explainer run winml analyze / perf / eval and paste the output' — violates the producer/tester split (_meta-007): the explainer running its own verification commands re-creates the self-grading loop the split exists to break.
findings.what_was_done: Split the responsibility along the existing producer/tester line. TESTER (tester.md): extended verdict_table so each ladder row carries the exact reproducible `command`, added a standalone `analysis` block (winml analyze op-level data: total_operators, unique_operator_types, per-EP classification, artifact path — captured once the L0 artifact exists, explicitly NOT a Goal tier), and a consolidated `reproducible_commands` list; added a 'Component/op-level analysis' how-to section. EXPLAINER (explainer.md): expanded the report from 9 to 12 items (10=perf&eval numbers lifted from L1/L3 rows, 11=op-level analyze data, 12=reproducible commands), and hardened the cardinal constraint to state the explainer never runs build/perf/analyze/eval — missing data goes back to the tester, it is never patched by the explainer running the command. Synced the '9 items' references in orchestrator.md, planner.md, reviewer.md to 12 and added the three new items (plus a fabrication-flag check) to the reviewer checklist.
findings.why_it_matters: PR reviewers and maintainers want performance, op-coverage, and a way to reproduce — front-and-center, not buried. But the value of the producer/tester split is that the agent WRITING the report is not the agent that RAN the verification. Routing the three new evidence blocks through the tester keeps that guarantee: the explainer stays a pure formatter, and the reviewer can flag any item 10–12 number that has no matching tester `verdict_table` row as a fabrication.
findings.rule_change: PR-description contract: the report is 12 items. Items 10 (perf & eval numbers), 11 (component/op-level winml analyze data), 12 (reproducible commands) are MANDATORY and are reformatted from the tester's verdict_table (ladder[].command, ladder[].evidence, analysis, reproducible_commands) into readable PR tables/bullets/command-blocks. FIDELITY-VS-PRESENTATION split: the explainer preserves every value byte-for-byte (no upgraded verdict, no rounded number) BUT must present them as legible markdown, NOT dump the raw verdict_table JSON into the PR body ('transcribe verbatim' = values unchanged, not 'paste the JSON'). The explainer NEVER runs winml build/perf/analyze/eval; a missing item is returned to the tester, never filled by the explainer running the command. Tester now owns capturing op-level analyze data + per-tier reproducible commands in addition to the Goal ladder; the verdict_table JSON is the wire format between tester and explainer, not the PR text.
findings.patch_site: n/a (skill methodology + agent-contract change; no CLI code touched).

findings.title: The review loop re-runs but NEVER ingests human PR comments: the reviewer's re-entry trigger is 'is my own reviewer.md checklist green', not 'are there open review threads on the PR', so external maintainer comments are structurally invisible — the loop can self-correct forever and still never see them. No agent ever runs `gh api .../comments` or queries reviewThreads.
findings.observation: PR microsoft/winml-cli#951 (ViLT VQA). Reviewer xieofxie left 3 line-level review comments on 2026-06-25 (all substantive: static pixel_values H/W silently restricts export to square 384x384 + the docstring justification is factually wrong; a `.vilt` import placed out of sort order that deterministically fails ruff I001 CI lint; recipe value_range [0,2] contradicts the PR's own reviewer note that mask-of-ones must be [1,2]). The agent-driven loop then re-ran MULTIPLE times through 2026-07-06 — the 2026-07-06T13:50 verdict says 'Independent re-march of the checklist against the pushed producer fix' (added pytest), and the 2026-07-06T14:04 verdict even SELF-CORRECTED a process error ('unit tests are NOT the Goal ladder') and re-marched L0/L1/L2. So the agent was alive, looping, and self-critical 11 days AFTER the comments landed — yet all 3 review threads remained isResolved=false, isOutdated=false (the cited lines were never touched) with zero agent replies. The loop was not 'too late' and did not 'end the session'; every iteration re-verified reviewer.md's OWN checklist items (pytest / Goal ladder / scope / coverage) and none of those items is 'enumerate open review threads from any author and confirm each is addressed'. Human comments were never in the scanned input set. Corollary blind spot: the deterministic ruff I001 failure was missed because reviewer.md has no `ruff check` gate AND the loop didn't read the comment that pointed at it — two independent blind spots covering one bug.
findings.what_was_done: Added an operational gate to reviewer.md (new load-bearing checklist section 'External review threads — enumerate and close') that, after the PR checkout, REQUIRES fetching every review + issue comment via `gh api repos/microsoft/winml-cli/pulls/<N>/comments` and the GraphQL reviewThreads(isResolved,isOutdated), listing every OPEN thread from ANY author (not just the in-loop reviewer), and mapping each to a producer fix + a thread reply and resolve before APPROVE. An open review thread from any commenter is REQUEST_CHANGES on its own, independent of whether the reviewer.md checklist is otherwise green. Also added a `uv run ruff check` gate (deterministic lint must pass — an import-order / I001 failure is REQUEST_CHANGES). Rewrote orchestrator.md Step 6b so the passive 'a maintainer leaves a new comment re-opens the loop' assertion now points at the concrete fetch command + names the reviewer as the owner that must run it every pass (not a hypothetical daemon).
findings.why_it_matters: The producer/tester/reviewer split (_meta-007) closes the SELF-grading hole, but it silently opened an EXTERNAL-grading hole: the loop grades itself against its own checklist and treats 'checklist green' as done, so real human review — the entire point of opening a PR — is dropped on the floor. A loop that re-runs and self-corrects but never reads the PR conversation is worse than one that stops, because it looks diligent (multiple verdicts, self-correction) while ignoring the reviewer. The fix makes 'read and close every external thread' a first-class, command-backed checklist item with a named owner, converting orchestrator Step 6b's aspirational 'watch' into an executed fetch.
findings.rule_change: Reviewer contract: before APPROVE, the reviewer MUST enumerate ALL open PR review threads via `gh api .../pulls/<N>/comments` + GraphQL reviewThreads and confirm each (from ANY author) is either resolved with a code fix or answered with an explicit, agreed rationale. Any open thread = REQUEST_CHANGES, regardless of checklist state. The re-entry trigger for the loop is now '(my checklist is green) AND (zero open external threads)', not the former '(my checklist is green)' alone. Additionally, `uv run ruff check` must pass — a deterministic lint failure (e.g. I001 import order) is REQUEST_CHANGES and MUST NOT depend on a human comment to be caught. orchestrator Step 6b's 'maintainer comment re-opens the loop' is now backed by the reviewer running the comment-fetch every pass.
findings.patch_site: n/a (skill methodology + agent-contract change; no CLI code touched).
findings.skill_edit: agents/reviewer.md (new 'External review threads — enumerate and close' checklist section with gh api + reviewThreads commands; new `ruff check` gate; re-entry-trigger wording); agents/orchestrator.md (Step 6b passive-watch -> concrete fetch command + reviewer ownership).

validated_on: microsoft/winml-cli#951 (ViLT VQA): 3 xieofxie review threads open+unaddressed 2026-06-25..2026-07-09 across >=2 agent re-march iterations; reviewThreads all isResolved=false/isOutdated=false; deterministic ruff I001 also missed for lack of a lint gate
