findings.title: Invoking the skill authorizes the full repair/review loop without permission pauses, but the PR remains draft
findings.observation: Dogfooding the hardened reviewer on microsoft/winml-cli#951, the agent halted TWICE: (1) right after the reviewer issued REQUEST_CHANGES it asked '要我现在发布吗? / 要我一并修吗?' instead of re-entering the producer; then after that was corrected, (2) it drove the producer fixes to green (ruff + pytest) but STOPPED AGAIN before `git push` + `gh pr comment`, asking the user to confirm those 'irreversible' steps. The user rejected BOTH pauses — the second explicitly: '请你修改skill，这个过程是不需要停下来等确认的'. The orchestrator.md contract ALREADY said REQUEST_CHANGES re-enters the producer and repeats until APPROVE/REJECT, and Step 0 preflight ALREADY front-loads the real host block. So the loop did not fail for lack of contract — it failed because the deference reflex kept re-attaching to whatever the next step was. My first patch drew the line at 'reversible → just do it, irreversible (push/comment/merge) → confirm once', but pushing to the PR's OWN branch and replying to threads on the PR ARE the loop's normal output; gating them on a human 'yes' re-creates the hand-crank the orchestrator exists to remove.
findings.what_was_done: Rewrote the orchestrator.md 'Do not pause for permission mid-loop' rule so planner/reviewer re-entry, local edits, ruff/pytest, pushes to this PR's branch, PR comments/reviews, thread resolution, and rebases proceed without asking. The original edit also authorized ready-state promotion, but `_meta-076` later superseded that one action: generated PRs remain draft after APPROVE. Pauses remain limited to terminal states and the non-convergence guard; destructive actions outside this PR's lifecycle still require a heads-up.
findings.why_it_matters: _meta-043 gave the loop an owner and _meta-056 gave it sight of human comments, but both are inert if the driver freezes before edits, pushes, comments, or thread resolution. Those actions are part of driving this PR to APPROVE and are pre-authorized; changing draft state is not part of the current loop, and destructive actions on shared state remain outside its standing authorization.
findings.rule_change: Invoking the skill authorizes the whole loop end-to-end: push to the PR's branch, comment/review, thread reply+resolve, and rebase proceed without permission pauses. The PR is created draft and remains draft after APPROVE; `gh pr ready` is forbidden by `_meta-076` and the current explainer/orchestrator contract.
findings.patch_site: n/a (skill methodology + agent-contract change; no CLI code touched).
findings.skill_edit: agents/orchestrator.md ('Do not pause for permission mid-loop' rule rewritten: whole-loop standing authorization incl. push/comment/resolve; reversible/irreversible table + confirm-before-push carve-out removed; heads-up narrowed to destructive out-of-lifecycle actions).

validated_on: microsoft/winml-cli#951 dogfood: agent halted twice (after REQUEST_CHANGES, then before push/comment); user rejected both, explicitly instructing the push/comment step needs no confirmation — the exact failure this finding names
falsified_on: my own first fix's premise that push/comment on the PR warrant a one-time confirm — user overruled it: driving the PR's own push/comment/resolve is pre-authorized loop work, not a shared-boundary stop
not_yet_tested_on: a fresh REQUEST_CHANGES where the orchestrator re-enters the producer, pushes the fix, replies+resolves every thread, and reaches APPROVE with ZERO permission-pauses anywhere in the loop

findings.mechanism_notes: Directly observed and user-confirmed twice in this session. Key correction: the deference reflex is not fixed by a reversible/irreversible taxonomy (it just re-attaches to the irreversible step); it is fixed by declaring the whole loop pre-authorized and carving out ONLY destructive out-of-lifecycle actions.
findings.resolution: Whole-loop standing authorization remains current for repair, push, comment, resolution, and rebase. `_meta-076` later removed draft-to-ready from the authorized lifecycle; APPROVE leaves the labeled PR in DRAFT.

findings.title: Recipe placement is a coverage-honesty contract, not a repo-mimicry choice: a recipe MUST be filed under one <ep>/<device>/ folder per EP it was ACTUALLY tested on, duplicated identically across each tested bucket, and NEVER flat and NEVER under an untested EP. Reinstates _meta-051 and supersedes _meta-054's flat-by-default correction.
findings.observation: In batch-6 the producer filed the M4/M5/M6 fp16 recipes FLAT (examples/recipes/<org>_<model>/<task>_<precision>_config.json), following _meta-054's 'flat is the live-repo norm (135/138 flat)' rule. The user pointed at examples/recipes/facebook_dinov2-base/qnn/npu/image-feature-extraction_w8a16_config.json and stated the convention directly (2026-07-13): 'put it under the corresponding EP. Whichever EPs you tested on, put it under those EPs (like my example), duplication is fine. Because you only tested on that one EP, you cannot guarantee the others work.' This reframes _meta-054's mistake: _meta-054 argued from DESCRIPTIVE repo state ('most existing recipes are flat, so flat is correct') but the user's rule is NORMATIVE and semantic ('the folder set is a map of VERIFIED coverage'). The two batch-6 recipes were validated on CPU only, so under _meta-058 they belong at .../cpu/cpu/, not flat and not under any NPU/GPU folder. Filing flat erases which EP the evidence covers; filing under an untested EP fabricates coverage.
findings.what_was_done: Reinstated the nested-per-EP layout as the ONLY correct placement and tightened it with a tested-only rule: (1) producer.md Step 3 Path bullet rewritten — always nest, duplicate the identical recipe under EVERY (ep,device) the tester PASSED and only those, never flat, never an untested EP; (2) reviewer.md L0-scope glob + recipe-exists box rewritten — flat (no <ep>/<device> segments) = REQUEST_CHANGES, an EP folder with no matching tester per_ep PASS = fabricated-coverage REQUEST_CHANGES, a PASSED EP with no folder = producer-gap REQUEST_CHANGES; the folder set must equal the verified-coverage set exactly; (3) tester.md per-EP-march bullet re-cited to _meta-058 with 'per_ep PASS set == shipped folder set' and 'flag a folder for an EP you couldn't exercise'; (4) explainer.md Lane B L0 glob re-cited to 'one folder per TESTED EP+device, never flat'. _template.json + learner.md already used the nested recipe_template (never reverted by _meta-054), so no change needed there.
findings.why_it_matters: A recipe's build/quantization/perf/accuracy is only proven on the EP it was actually run on — EP-specific fusion/opset/quant levers that win on QNN NPU can reverse on QNN GPU, hang on quantized GPU, or regress on CPU (the auto-config evidence corpus behind _meta-051). So the set of <ep>/<device>/ folders is not cosmetic: it is the honest, structural record of which EPs the contribution actually verified. Flat placement throws that information away; placing under an untested EP asserts coverage that was never measured. Encoding tested-EP-in-path makes the reviewer able to verify coverage by folder presence and keeps a CPU-only contribution from silently reading as all-EP.
findings.rule_change: Recipes ALWAYS live at examples/recipes/<org>_<model>/<ep>/<device>/<task>_<precision>_config.json. The producer files one folder per (ep,device) the tester validated on, duplicating the identical recipe across each, and NONE for untested EPs. Flat = REQUEST_CHANGES. An EP folder without a matching tester per_ep PASS = REQUEST_CHANGES (fabricated coverage). A tested-and-PASSED EP with no folder = REQUEST_CHANGES (producer gap). Supersedes _meta-054's flat-by-default rule; the current in-tree flatness is legacy, not the target.

findings.title: Op-level `winml analyze` data has NO valid N/A once the L0 build PASSED: a successful build means the artifact exists, so analyze is always runnable and 'deferred/host-availability/not-run' for item 11 is a fail-closed REQUEST_CHANGES, not an honest N/A.
findings.observation: PRs #1094 (audeering/wav2vec2-large-robust-24-ft-age-gender, audio-classification fp16) and #1095 (MahmoudAshraf/mms-300m-1130-forced-aligner, ASR fp16) both shipped with fp16 build exit 0, structural L0 data, and CPU perf (P50) numbers — but ZERO op-level analyze data (item 11 of the 12-item report entirely absent), and eval reduced to a bare 'not confirmed' with no cited CLI-BLOCKED error. The user asked why the agreed description contract (perf & eval data / per-component op-level data / reproducible cmd) was not honored. Root cause is NOT that op-level data was unobtainable: build succeeded, the artifact was in hand, and `winml analyze -m <out>/model.onnx --ep all` runs on any built .onnx with no further prerequisite beyond the one-time runtime-rules download (_meta-013). It was simply skipped, then waved off like the genuinely-blocked items (non-CPU EPs = host availability, L3 = dataset unconfirmed). The skill already required item 11 everywhere (tester captures it, explainer item 11, reviewer 12-item box) but the reviewer's blanket 'even as N/A — see ...' escape let a PASS-build PR omit it without penalty. Sending review comments only fixes these two PRs (治标); the structural fix is closing the N/A loophole for the one item that is always obtainable post-build.
findings.rule_change: Op-level analyze (item 11) is MANDATORY whenever the L0 build PASSED and has no valid N/A. Because any perf/eval number presupposes a built artifact, ANY PR carrying L0 PASS (or perf/eval data) with item 11 empty/'deferred'/'not run'/'host availability' is REQUEST_CHANGES, routed to the TESTER (not producer) to run `winml analyze --ep all` and repopulate verdict_table.analysis. The ONLY accepted no-counts state is a genuinely-unavailable rule set (source tree pre-download → exit 2 'No runtime rule parquet files were found', or offline/no gh auth), which MUST be cited verbatim. All-unknown rows for CPU/CUDA/DML/MIGraphX are expected (no rules shipped) and are NOT 'missing data'; the accelerator rows (NvTensorRTRTX/OpenVINO/QNN/VitisAI) are the real coverage signal. Distinct from legitimately-blocked items: non-CPU EP perf (host availability) and L3 eval (unsupported task / dataset) CAN be HOST-BLOCKED/CLI-BLOCKED with cited evidence — op-level analyze cannot, once the build passed.

findings.title: Recipe vs code fix is a per-model-vs-class-of-models decision, not a size-of-diff decision: an override derivable from published metadata by a rule that generalizes to a whole class of models belongs in data-driven auto-config code (Lane A), while a per-checkpoint declaration belongs in a recipe — and a single-model code branch (`if model_type/model_id == "..."`) is a disguised recipe that is always rejected.
findings.observation: Human reviewer (xieofxie) asked on both PR #1094 and #1095 'if without the config, could perf run it directly?' and then 'should we update the code to make it work?'. The two look identical (both are recipe-only PRs whose baseline build FAILS without the recipe) but the honest answers differ. #1095 (MahmoudAshraf/mms-300m-1130-forced-aligner, ASR) fails because winml's ASR auto-loader is hard-wired to AutoModelForSpeechSeq2Seq and rejects Wav2Vec2Config; the recipe pins loader.model_class=AutoModelForCTC. That override is derivable from config.json (architectures=['Wav2Vec2ForCTC']) by a rule — `architectures[] endswith 'ForCTC' -> AutoModelForCTC` — that generalizes to the ENTIRE CTC-ASR family and misfires on nothing, so it is a class-of-models gap that should be fixed in code (the recipe should degrade to a regression fixture). #1094 (audeering/wav2vec2-large-robust-24-ft-age-gender, audio-classification) fails because a custom trust_remote_code AgeGenderModel with architectures=['Model'] auto-resolves to text-classification; the recipe pins task=audio-classification. That value is NOT derivable from metadata — the class name 'Model' carries no task signal and only a human knows the intent — so the recipe IS the root primitive and any 'code fix' could only be an if-this-one-repo hardcode. The skill had a recipe lane and a Lane-A code lane but no explicit criterion for choosing between them, so #1095 was mis-scoped as L0-recipe when it is really an L1 code fix.
findings.rule_change: Planner Step 1b runs a reducibility test after the baseline gate: name the exact auto-config decision the fix overrides (task, loader.model_class, loader family, opset_version, eval.dataset, EP option), then ask whether the correct value is derivable from the model's own published metadata (architectures / model_type / pipeline_tag) by a rule that generalizes to a whole class of models WITHOUT misfiring on others. YES => class-of-models gap => fix the code (Effort >= L1, Lane A on winml-cli), data-driven, so `winml build -m <id>` works with no recipe; the recipe (if any) degrades to a regression fixture. NO => per-model declaration (human intent, custom trust_remote_code model, several legally-valid answers, a per-checkpoint dataset/opset choice) => the recipe is the right primitive (Effort L0/L0*). Cardinal-Rule-1 guardrail: a 'code fix' that recognizes a single model id/name (if model_type == '...', if model_id == '...', if '...' in name) is NOT a fix — it is a recipe smuggled into source and is always rejected; class fixes are always data-driven. The decision is frozen in charter.fix_class { override, kind, derivable_from_metadata, generalization_key, resolution }.
findings.patch_site: n/a (skill methodology / scope-triage change; the downstream winml-cli code fix for the #1095 class — deriving AutoModelForCTC from architectures — is a separate Lane-A/product change, not part of this skill edit).

findings.title: A recipe is ALWAYS the deliverable and Goal must aim as high as reachable: a passing baseline does NOT mean 'no contribution' (reverses _meta-038's catalog-clone conclusion) because a checked-in <ep>/<device> recipe is a verified-coverage claim the out-of-the-box CPU auto-build never establishes. Baseline sets the Goal FLOOR (aim strictly above it), generates the STARTING recipe via `winml config`, and the recipe-vs-config diff is now documentation, not a reject gate.
findings.observation: The user directed three linked changes to the planner methodology on 2026-07-14: (1) GOAL should climb as high as reachable unless genuinely unreachable — e.g. if the baseline already builds (L0), the committed Goal ceiling must be at least L1 (perf), not L0; (2) OUTCOME — a recipe is now always considered necessary, even when the baseline already builds, because verifying/testing the model on a specific EP is itself meaningful, so all 'no gain / not a contribution / catalog clone / file_pr=false / short-circuit to explainer' language must go; (3) the baseline should GENERATE the recipe via `winml config`, and the explainer/reviewer should DIFF the shipped recipe against that auto-config output to determine and document the change. This directly reverses the headline conclusion of _meta-038 ('6/6 recent recipe PRs had zero engineering delta -> catalog clones -> do not file'): under the new policy those PRs would still be filed as verified-coverage artifacts for their tested EP, with the identical-to-auto-config diff stated plainly rather than used as a rejection. The empirical diff machinery of _meta-038 is kept but repurposed from gatekeeping to documentation.
findings.rule_change: PLANNER: charter.catalog_gate (baseline_build/verdict/file_pr) is replaced by charter.baseline (build/config_recipe/goal_floor); the file_pr short-circuit hard rule and the 'catalog clone -> do not file / hand to explainer' path are removed — the only non-filing case is a genuine duplicate of an already-checked-in recipe for the same (model, task, ep, device, precision). New ceiling-selection rule: commit the HIGHEST reachable Goal tier; baseline sets the floor (builds -> ceiling >= L1; perfs -> aim L2/L3); stop climbing only when the next tier is genuinely unreachable (CLI gap / no dataset / all higher EPs host-blocked); 'a lower tier already passed' is never a reason to cap. Step 1b retitled 'Baseline probe (measure main's support level + generate the starting recipe)' and gains a `winml config -m <id> [-t <task>] [--model-class <cls>] [--trust-remote-code] -o temp/baseline_<stem>` step whose output is the producer's starting recipe and the diff anchor. done-when now requires goal_ceiling strictly above baseline.goal_floor unless every higher tier is unreachable. EXPLAINER: report item 1 now carries the recipe-vs-`winml config` diff (two-file JSON comparison, strip _note, not a winml run) stating identical-vs-changed fields. REVIEWER: baseline check flips — a passing baseline is NOT REQUEST_CHANGES; instead require the diff to be present + honest and require the Goal ceiling to have climbed above the inherited floor (L0-only headline on a builds-on-main model = mis-scope = REQUEST_CHANGES to raise the ceiling). SKILL.md three-axes section gains the aim-high + recipe-always principle; Step 1b labels updated.

findings.title: 'Aim as high as reachable' (_meta-061) must be measured against the TEST HOST: L2 (numeric-vs-PyTorch, a local CPU script) and L3 (winml eval on a dataset, CPU-runnable whenever the task has one) are host-reachable on any CPU box, so capping the Goal at L1 and 'deferring L2/L3 to CI' is under-reach, not a legitimate stop. 'Defer to CI' is valid ONLY for accelerator-hardware tiers the host lacks (NPU/GPU-EP perf & eval) — never for CPU-runnable numeric/eval tiers.
findings.observation: Re-running the 10-PR batch (winml-cli #1068/#952/#951/#1018/#1094/#1095/#1096/#1099/#1100/#1101) through the _meta-061-hardened skill on 2026-07-14 confirmed the new touchpoints are applied (recipes are nested per tested EP per _meta-058, baseline cites `winml config`, PR bodies carry a recipe-vs-autoconf diff, the reviewer no longer rejects a passing baseline as a catalog clone). But three PRs — #1099 (usyd-community/vitpose-plus-huge, keypoint-detection; COCO-keypoints dataset exists), #1100 (deepset/roberta-large-squad2, question-answering; SQuAD v2 dataset exists), #1101 (google/owlv2-base-patch16) — ran only CPU L0+L1 and then wrote 'per-EP L2/L3 eval deferred to CI' / 'per-EP CI eval to confirm', capping the headline Goal at L1. Under _meta-061's aim-high rule that is under-reach: L2 (cosine/max-abs vs PyTorch) is a local script that always runs on CPU (planner Goal-axis already says L2 is 'script-based'), and L3 for #1099/#1100 has a real dataset that `winml eval` runs on CPU. The tiers were host-REACHABLE and were punted to CI anyway. The gap is that _meta-061's ceiling rule listed the legitimate stops ('CLI gap / no dataset / all higher EPs host-blocked') but never said 'CPU makes L2 always reachable and L3 reachable when a dataset exists', and the reviewer's aim-high box only enforced 'baseline builds => ceiling >= L1' — so an L1-capped PR that defers CPU-reachable L2/L3 to CI passed the check. 'Defer to CI' had become an escape hatch that caps the Goal below what the test host can actually verify.
findings.rule_change: PLANNER (ceiling-selection rule + Step 1b floor table): define 'reachable' against the CURRENT test host. The host's CPU makes L0 (build), L1 (CPU perf), and L2 (numeric-vs-PyTorch script) ALWAYS reachable, and L3 (winml eval) reachable whenever the task has a dataset (subset if it times out at scale, per _meta-029). The committed Goal ceiling must be the highest of these host-reachable tiers, not L1-by-default. 'Deferred to CI / to appropriate hardware' is legitimate ONLY for accelerator-EP perf & eval the host cannot run (no NPU/GPU present) — it is NEVER a valid reason to skip CPU-runnable L2 or CPU-runnable L3. A charter that stops at L1 while L2 (always) or L3 (dataset exists) is CPU-reachable is mis-scoped. TESTER: the L0..ceiling march must run CPU-reachable L2 and L3 on the test host; recording them as 'deferred to CI' when they run on CPU is a march omission, not a HOST-BLOCKED. REVIEWER (aim-high box): replace 'baseline builds => headline Goal >= L1' with 'headline Goal == the highest host-reachable tier'; a PR that ran only L1 on CPU while L2 (always CPU-runnable) or L3 (task has a dataset) was skipped/'deferred to CI' is REQUEST_CHANGES to march the reachable tiers — CI-deferral is accepted only for accelerator-EP tiers with a cited get_available_providers() snapshot proving the hardware is absent.

findings.skill_edit: agents/planner.md (Goal-axis ceiling-selection rule + Step 1b floor table: 'reachable' defined against the test host; CPU makes L2 always + L3 dataset-dependent reachable; CI-deferral only for absent accelerator hardware). agents/reviewer.md (aim-high box: enforce highest-host-reachable-tier, not just >= L1; CPU-reachable L2/L3 deferred to CI = REQUEST_CHANGES). agents/tester.md (march covers CPU-reachable L2/L3; 'deferred to CI' for a CPU-runnable tier is an omission, not HOST-BLOCKED).

findings.title: Historical CPU-only review exposed the need for carried-over EP evidence; host-unreachable folders are not trusted without provenance
findings.observation: Re-running the 10-PR batch under the _meta-062-hardened skill, model 1 (facebook/bart-large-mnli, PR #1068) was verified on a CPU-only host — `get_available_providers()` returns `['CPUExecutionProvider']` only, no DML/OpenVINO/QNN/TensorRT. The branch ships six EP buckets (cpu/cpu, dml/gpu, openvino/{cpu,gpu,npu}, qnn/npu). The CPU ladder passed cleanly on this host (L0 build 195s, L1 perf P50 2551ms, L2 numeric vs PyTorch cosine 1.0000, L3 MNLI acc 0.90). But _meta-058's reviewer rule — 'the recipe must appear under exactly the (ep,device) buckets the tester validated on ... the folder set must equal the verified-coverage set exactly — no more (fabrication), no less (gap)' — forces REQUEST_CHANGES to DELETE the five accelerator buckets, because the tester only PASSed CPU on this host. That is wrong: those buckets are legitimate carried-over coverage verified on capable hardware in earlier runs, and deleting them on a CPU-only box destroys real, previously-established coverage. The rule mistook 'this host cannot re-verify EP X' for 'EP X coverage is fabricated'. A CPU-only reviewer must not be able to strip a model's NPU/GPU coverage simply by re-reviewing it on a machine that lacks those accelerators.
findings.rule_change: Current `_meta-073` contract: a host-unreachable tuple may be `CARRIED-OVER` only with auditable prior capable-host evidence for the exact `(ep, device, precision)` plus provider provenance. Absence of local hardware is not grounds to delete proven coverage, but it is never permission to trust an unproven folder by default.

Under _meta-058 the reviewer would REQUEST_CHANGES to delete dml/openvino/qnn buckets that a prior capable-hardware run had established. findings.title: A recipe's `loader.trust_remote_code: true` is NOT auto-applied by `winml build/perf/eval`: the operator MUST pass the CLI `--trust-remote-code` flag explicitly, or the build hard-fails 'contains custom code ... pass trust_remote_code=True'. The recipe field alone does not propagate. (Extends _meta-041, which covered only the missing flag on `inspect`.)
findings.observation: Live 10-PR re-run 2026-07-15, model #1018 (baidu/Unlimited-OCR, a DeepSeek-OCR-clone VLM whose config lives in a remote auto_map / custom modeling_*.py). The shipped recipe already carries `loader.trust_remote_code: true`, yet `winml build -m baidu/Unlimited-OCR -c <recipe>` (no CLI flag) FAILS with 'The repository ... contains custom code which must be executed ... Please pass the argument trust_remote_code=True to allow custom code to be run.' The build only succeeds when `--trust-remote-code` is added to the CLI (L0 then PASSes, 391.3s). The clean-main baseline (no recipe) fails identically, so the gap is real either way. So even with a correct recipe, a producer/tester who trusts the recipe loader field and omits the CLI flag will read the failure as a model-coverage gap rather than a missing-flag operator error.
findings.rule_change: PRODUCER/TESTER (build/perf/eval invocation): for any model whose HF repo requires trust_remote_code (auto_map / custom modeling_*.py, or a recipe with `loader.trust_remote_code: true`), ALWAYS pass `--trust-remote-code` on every `winml build`, `winml perf`, and `winml eval` command line - the recipe's loader field does NOT substitute for the CLI flag. Treat a 'contains custom code ... pass trust_remote_code=True' failure as this missing-flag operator error, never as model-coverage evidence. REVIEWER: a recipe carrying `loader.trust_remote_code: true` whose PR body's reproduction commands omit `--trust-remote-code` is an un-reproducible command block = REQUEST_CHANGES.
findings.patch_site: Candidate winml-cli improvement (out of scope for the model PRs, note only): have the build/perf/eval commands honor `loader.trust_remote_code` from the resolved recipe as a default for the flag, so a recipe that declares custom code does not also require the CLI flag. Until then this is an operator-discipline finding.

findings.title: A recipe's `quant.mode: "fp16"` is SILENTLY OVERRIDDEN by CPU auto-precision (cpu -> fp32): to actually get an fp16 artifact you MUST pass the CLI `--precision fp16` explicitly. Also CORRECTS the stale note that '`winml build` does NOT accept `--precision`' - build DOES accept `--precision` as of v0.2.0.
findings.observation: Live 10-PR re-run 2026-07-15, models #1094 (audeering/wav2vec2-age-gender), #1095 (MahmoudAshraf/mms-forced-aligner), #1096 (impira/layoutlm-invoices) - each recipe sets `quant.mode: "fp16"`. Building with the recipe alone (`winml build -m <id> -c <recipe>`) produces a full-size fp32 model.onnx.data (e.g. #1095 1203.4 MB) and perf reports 'Model Precision: fp32'; the recipe's fp16 request is dropped because the CPU device's auto-precision resolves to fp32 and wins. Adding `--precision fp16` yields the correct half-size fp16 artifact (#1095 601.7 MB, perf 'Model Precision: fp16'). Separately, this falsifies the earlier hint (user_skill findings, line ~1007, 'verified 2026-06-23') that `winml build` rejects `--precision` - the flag is accepted and is in fact REQUIRED to honor a recipe's fp16 intent on CPU.
findings.rule_change: PRODUCER/TESTER: when a recipe declares `quant.mode: "fp16"` (or the Goal targets an fp16 artifact), ALWAYS pass `--precision fp16` on the `winml build` CLI and CONFIRM the output by (a) model.onnx.data being ~half the fp32 size and (b) `winml perf` printing 'Model Precision: fp16'. Do NOT assume the recipe's quant.mode alone produced fp16 - on CPU it is overridden to fp32. REVIEWER: an fp16-claiming PR whose artifact size / perf 'Model Precision' shows fp32, or whose build command omits `--precision fp16`, is REQUEST_CHANGES. Delete/ignore any legacy guidance that says build has no --precision flag.
findings.patch_site: Candidate winml-cli improvement (note only): recipe-declared quant.mode should not be silently overridden by device auto-precision; either honor the recipe or warn loudly. Until then, the explicit CLI flag is the workaround.

Remove the stale 'build has no --precision' note.

findings.title: A recipe-only PR can SILENTLY export a RANDOM-initialized-head model when the checkpoint's architecture does not map to a standard HF Auto class AND the repo ships no trust_remote_code modeling_*.py: HF falls back to a generic class and re-inits the task head, so the ONNX is syntactically valid but numerically meaningless. The L2 numeric-vs-PyTorch gate is what catches it (and it can NEVER pass, because both the ref and the export load different random heads).
findings.observation: Live 10-PR re-run 2026-07-15, model #1094 (audeering/wav2vec2-large-robust-24-ft-age-gender). config `architectures: ['Model']` (audeering's custom AgeGenderModel) but the HF repo has NO trust_remote_code modeling_*.py. So `AutoModelForAudioClassification` cannot find 'Model', falls back to the standard `Wav2Vec2ForSequenceClassification`, and emits 'Some weights ... were newly initialized: classifier.{weight,bias}, projector.{weight,bias} ... you should probably TRAIN this model'. Both the PyTorch reference AND the winml export therefore load DIFFERENT random heads on each load, so L2 cosine is garbage (fp32 cos 0.67, fp16 cos 0.30) and can never converge. Build (L0) and perf (L1) both 'pass' - the defect is invisible without a numeric check. A recipe-only contribution cannot fix this (needs a Lane-A custom loader that maps audeering's 'Model' head weights, or the model is out of scope).
findings.rule_change: PRODUCER/TESTER: after build, ALWAYS scan the model-load logs for the HF 'Some weights ... were newly initialized ... you should probably TRAIN' warning; if present, the export has a RANDOM head and any downstream perf/accuracy is meaningless. This happens when `config.architectures` names a non-standard class (e.g. bare 'Model') with no trust_remote_code modeling_*.py to supply it. L2 (numeric vs PyTorch) is MANDATORY for such models and will fail by construction - report the FAIL with root cause, do NOT paper over it. A recipe-only (Lane B) PR cannot resolve a random-head model; escalate to Lane A (custom loader mapping the real head weights) or mark the model out-of-scope. REVIEWER: an audio/text/vision-classification PR that ran only L0+L1, whose model emits the 'newly initialized head' warning, and that omits L2, is REQUEST_CHANGES (the coverage is fabricated - the head is random).
findings.patch_site: n/a for the model PR (upstream model-packaging issue); a Lane-A custom loader mapping the checkpoint's real head tensors would be the fix if the model is in scope.
findings.skill_edit: agents/tester.md (post-build log scan for HF 'newly initialized head / should probably TRAIN' warning => random-head export, L2 mandatory and expected-FAIL, report honestly). agents/producer.md (Lane B cannot fix a non-standard architectures+no-modeling.py checkpoint; escalate to Lane A or out-of-scope). agents/reviewer.md (L0+L1-only PR whose model shows the random-head warning without L2 = REQUEST_CHANGES).

findings.title: Historical OWLv2 input misbinding motivated current generalized keyword-name resolution and mandatory named-input validation
findings.observation: Live 10-PR re-run 2026-07-15, model #1101 (google/owlv2-base-patch16, zero-shot-object-detection). The recipe declared `input_tensors` as [pixel_values, input_ids, attention_mask], but OWLv2's forward signature is (input_ids, pixel_values, attention_mask, ...). torch.onnx.export zipped the recipe's names onto graph inputs in forward order, so the exported ONNX had input 'pixel_values' = int32 [1,16] (actually the text ids) and 'input_ids' = float [1,3,960,960] (actually the image). L0 build 'passed' and the mislabel was invisible until `winml perf --input-data <npz>` (feeding by name) crashed: 'Invalid rank for input: pixel_values Got: 4 Expected: 2'. Reordering the recipe's input_tensors to (input_ids, pixel_values, attention_mask) and rebuilding produced correctly-labeled inputs; L2 vs PyTorch then passed all four outputs at cos 1.000000.
findings.rule_change: CURRENT MAIN: keyword-invoked inputs are resolved from a complete unambiguous `forward()` signature, while explicit positional `get_export_args` protocols retain their declared order. Recipe order alone is not authoritative. PRODUCER preserves the invocation protocol; TESTER feeds by name and validates every exported name against shape/dtype; REVIEWER requests resolver/protocol diagnosis on mismatch rather than prescribing recipe reordering without proof of positional invocation.
findings.patch_site: Implemented by the generalized `_resolve_keyword_input_names` repair merged in winml-cli #1155. Preserve explicit positional protocols and keep named-input artifact validation as the regression detector.
findings.skill_edit: agents/producer.md, agents/tester.md, and agents/reviewer.md now distinguish keyword resolution from explicit positional protocols and require named input-spec validation.

validated_on: live re-run 2026-07-15: google/owlv2-base-patch16 #1101 - recipe input order [pixel_values,input_ids,...] mislabeled the ONNX inputs; perf crashed 'Invalid rank for input: pixel_values Got 4 Expected 2'; reorder to forward order fixed it, L2 cos 1.000000 x4 outputs
falsified_on: Current winml-cli main after #1155: OWLv2 and OwlViT keyword inputs bind correctly even when recipe input_tensors order differs from forward(); see owlv2-004 and owlvit-001

findings.mechanism_notes: Confirmed by inspecting the built model twice: mis-ordered recipe -> 'pixel_values' int32[1,16] + 'input_ids' float[1,3,960,960] (swapped); reordered recipe -> 'input_ids' int32[1,16] + 'pixel_values' float[1,3,960,960] (correct). Single-input models are immune; the defect only bites multi-input models where the recipe order differs from forward order.
findings.resolution: Historical #1101 workaround retained as evidence. Current contract follows #1155's generalized keyword resolver, preserves explicit positional protocols, and validates final ONNX bindings by name/shape/dtype.

findings.title: Canonicalize CARRIED-OVER for host-unreachable L0 recipe tuples and ANALYZE-PARTIAL-SUCCESS for complete analyze JSON emitted alongside a non-zero host-plugin error
findings.observation: The PR #951 ViLT tester correctly followed _meta-063 by recording host-unreachable OpenVINO/QNN L0 recipe tuples as CARRIED-OVER, but the canonical Goal verdict tables in planner/tester/reviewer still enumerated only PASS, CLI-BLOCKED, HOST-BLOCKED, and FAIL. The prose already required CARRIED-OVER, so the wire vocabulary contradicted its own methodology. The same run exposed a separate supplementary-analysis state: `winml analyze --ep all` emitted complete, parseable JSON with 440 operators, 17 types, and all six requested EP classifications, then exited 1 because the installed OpenVINO plugin could not load missing onnxruntime_providers_shared.dll (Error 126). Treating this as either ordinary success or unusable FAIL loses evidence. Because analyze is explicitly not a Goal tier, ANALYZE-PARTIAL-SUCCESS belongs in `analysis.status`, not in ladder verdicts.
findings.rule_change: GOAL/PER-TUPLE VOCABULARY: add CARRIED-OVER as an L0 `per_ep[]` verdict only for a shipped recipe folder whose EP is absent from the current host; require the provider snapshot and a statement that coverage was prior-verified elsewhere. It is neither a fresh PASS nor an L1/L3 substitute (unreachable runtime tuples remain HOST-BLOCKED). ANALYSIS VOCABULARY: add `analysis.status = ANALYZE-PARTIAL-SUCCESS` when the output JSON is parseable and complete for the requested EP set despite a non-zero exit caused by host/plugin registration. Preserve exit code and exact error; never infer runtime support from rule rows. Missing/truncated JSON remains analysis failure/incomplete evidence.

findings.title: A background watchdog preserves execution but does not satisfy a user-visible continuous-progress requirement

Repository/PR heartbeat comments remain prohibited unless useful—the visibility requirement applies to the user conversation and internal run ledger, not noisy GitHub comments.

findings.title: Checkpoint generation defaults can violate static ONNX shape contracts, and inference failures must not be downgraded to skipped Eval rows
findings.observation: The first real opus-mt-fr-en translation smoke inherited Marian's default num_beams=4. The repaired path derives encoder/decode capacities from ONNX metadata, truncates source input, uses deterministic num_beams=1, caps max_new_tokens at cache capacity minus the initial token, propagates tokenizer/runtime/inference exceptions, and only skips malformed dataset/output values with exact attempted/evaluated/skipped accounting.

findings.title: Building a quant recipe with explicit `--device`/`--precision` overrides can silently clear `config.quant`, yielding a successful build of the wrong precision
findings.observation: First tester pass for `impira/layoutlm-document-qa` built `examples/recipes/impira_layoutlm-document-qa/question-answering_w8a16_config.json` with explicit CPU overrides (`winml build -c ...question-answering_w8a16_config.json -m impira/layoutlm-document-qa -o temp\impira_layoutlm-document-qa\w8a16 --ep cpu --device cpu --rebuild`) and concluded the recipe emitted fp32: the resulting `temp\impira_layoutlm-document-qa\w8a16\winml_build_config.json` showed `"quant": null`, `temp\impira_layoutlm-document-qa\perf_w8a16_cli.log` printed `Model Precision: fp32`, and the old `l0_validate.log` histogram contained no UINT8/UINT16 initializers. This was a methodology trap, not a model bug. Reading `src\winml\modelkit\commands\build.py:660-672` shows the mechanism: whenever `--device` or `--precision` is explicitly CLI-provided, build patches quant/compile policy and clears `cfg.quant` if the resolved policy is fp32/none. The corrected rerun built the SAME w8a16 recipe *recipe-driven* (no `--device`, no `--precision`) and preserved `quant={mode: static, weight_type: uint8, activation_type: uint16}`, emitted UINT8/UINT16 initializers, and restored an honest quant-verification path. The orchestrator also reproduced the same silent de-quantization on a known-good control (`distilbert...question-answering_w8a16_config.json`), proving this is CLI methodology debt rather than LayoutLM-specific behavior.

Honest precision evidence for a quant recipe needs both the preserved `winml_build_config.json` quant block and a post-build artifact check (dtype histogram or the perf header's reported precision).

findings.title: Bounded Eval requires deterministic seeded selection and composite row/media provenance
findings.observation: Polish #1207 charter-r3 found that a successful CTC Eval could silently score the wrong rows. google/fleurs@70bb2e84b976b7e960aa89f1c648e09c59f894dd pl_pl/validation has 122 repeated sentence-ID values because distinct speaker recordings can share a transcription. The non-streaming path sorted the full split by this semantic `id` and selected IDs [1510,1510], while the streaming path preserved source order and selected [1525,1657]. Both rows were valid recordings and inference could produce finite metrics, so ordinary exit-code, metric, and processed-count checks would not expose the selection drift. Dependency e633f2e5c33d1784e311116f0e86a2bd0bd8a074 repaired selection order and source-index provenance, but independent review of stacked PR #1343 found the row identity contract remained incomplete: missing or boolean dataset IDs, missing audio paths, and duplicate audio paths all reached inference. Repaired dependency head 0d242174c25c062a21d40dceb645eace21a3f888 requires a nonnegative unique source index, valid JSON-stable scalar dataset ID, and stable redacted audio key or basename for each selected row; it rejects duplicate normalized media identities before inference while retaining legitimate duplicate semantic IDs. Independent review of PR #1335 then found a second silent selection defect: CTC Eval ignored `DatasetConfig.shuffle` and `seed` and always selected first-N. Exact repair head 3402b7b4b1990a0932551a3d69d3838df0e70bda attaches original indices before reordering and uses one seeded bounded-buffer shuffle-before-take path for streaming and non-streaming datasets. Exact-head probes repeated seed 123, distinguished seed 456, matched selected original indices in both modes below and beyond the 1000-row buffer, consumed an infinite-style source finitely, preserved the composite identity matrix, and closed under a PASS/CLOSED public seal.
findings.rule_change: Bounded Eval uses source-row authority unless the frozen dataset contract proves another ordering. Semantic IDs are never presumed unique and cannot sort or deduplicate bounded selection. Apply `DatasetConfig.shuffle` and `seed` before truncating to the requested sample count. For `shuffle=false`, streaming and non-streaming must select the same first-N source rows. For `shuffle=true`, both modes must use equivalent bounded-buffer semantics, reproduce the same original source-index selection for a fixed seed below and beyond the buffer size, distinguish different seeds, and consume an unbounded source only through the finite buffer plus requested prefix. Attach original source indices before any reordering and preserve them in emitted provenance. Tester emits requested/selected/processed/rejected/skipped accounting and a composite identity for every selected row: nonnegative source index, valid scalar dataset ID, and stable redacted media key/basename. Repeated semantic IDs remain valid when source and media identities differ. Missing or malformed identity components, duplicate source indices, and duplicate normalized media keys/basenames fail before inference with zero inference calls. Reviewer independently verifies these properties and rejects ignored shuffle configuration, mode drift, unbounded materialization, post-inference validation, deduplication, or silent row dropping.

findings.title: A stage-disable flag needs sink-level negative evidence, not parser acceptance
findings.observation: The openai/whisper-medium baseline at winml-cli main f831830c accepted `winml build ... --no-optimize` but still executed the Optimize stage. Producer traced the active Rich CLI paths and repaired `_build_hf_pipeline` and `_build_onnx_pipeline` so `--no-optimize` and config `skip_optimize` reached the actual optimization-stage sink; focused build regressions then passed at candidate c07a51ac. Existing `_meta-096` required planner stage-intent tracing for large post-export failures, but producer and reviewer contracts did not require retained negative evidence that a requested bypass actually suppressed its stage.
findings.rule_change: Whenever a contribution changes or relies on a stage-control bypass, producer retains a focused regression plus build-stage trace/log proving the disabled stage is absent and every independent requested stage still runs. Reviewer rejects CLI acceptance, help text, or resolved configuration as substitutes for evidence at the executing sink.

findings.title: Producer handoff must run every workflow-defined static check before first push
findings.observation: The initial openai/whisper-medium candidate 1d2a2eac reported Ruff, focused tests, and broad unit coverage as passing, but omitted the workflow-required whole-package command `uv run mypy -p winml.modelkit`. GitHub lint then found an incompatible `prepare_pipeline` return override in the new ASR evaluator. Producer repaired only typing at c07a51ac, where whole-package mypy passed for 445 source files. Tester and reviewer already required CI-parity checks later, but producer's pre-push handoff contract did not, allowing an avoidable red draft and repair cycle.
findings.rule_change: Before first push or handoff, producer reads the current PR workflows, runs every non-hardware static command on the candidate tree, and records exact commands/results in compatibility evidence. For WinML CLI this includes both whole-tree Ruff and `mypy -p winml.modelkit`; touched-file checks are not substitutes. Reviewer audits that timing and routes a first post-push discovery to learner even after repair.
